threads.title: Negative IOB : shouldn't be used in insulin calculations

comments.body:
Another experience for me with -IOB :

Started TT for exercise, but ended up working more then intended. 
Situation is 0 COB, bg flat 100 with -0.45 IOB. TT ended and AAPS immediately started to compensate for the negative IOB and sent me straight to Hypo. 
I could have avoided that but TT again etc, but also the compensation for -IOB is completely not logic since like @robertrub said, -IOB = 0 IOB, if ∆ is not high, which in my case average ∆ was -1, can't find a reason to have insulin.

Negative IOB is required in oref algorithm.
If you want to disable it in wizard dialog, first disable COB (GA) in your screenshot...

I don't know how negative IOB is used/useful in in OREF but the result is not good. We are obliged to cheat with high TT to prevent hypos which adds more neg IOB...

I don't know what would change deactivating COB as it was 0 on my screen capture and unchecking it doesn't uncheck IOB. Once more, this is a cheat to counteract an incorrect reaction of AAPS.

When autosens lowers to say 80% does anyone know what iob is calculated with respect to?  Is it 100% basal or 80% basal?  I've asked previously but got no replies as if 100% then changing to 80% could help, or could autosens say bleed iob another way (like cob decay) after a while?  For me I swing around plus or minus iob so 'think' settings are not too far off and autosens copes quite well with my variability but I quite often manually disconnect pump to 'help' -ve or 'prime' for +ve to hide from AAPS calculation. Just off the wall thoughts if rubbish as I don't know OREF workings please ignore.

> I don't know how negative IOB is used/useful in in OREF but the result is not good. We are obliged to cheat with high TT to prevent hypos which adds more neg IOB...
> 
> I don't know what would change deactivating COB as it was 0 on my screen capture and unchecking it doesn't uncheck IOB. Once more, this is a cheat to counteract an incorrect reaction of AAPS.

By cheating we get even more -iob

My answer was not to cheat, but to include or not negative IOB in wizard calculation. (after wizard you have a bolus so no more negative iob, it's just a way to limit risks of over dosing the bolus).

Negative IOB is not bad when all your settings are good. If you look in detail all your IOB curves during a perfect night with a flat BG curve glued to your target. you will see that your IOB vary between positive and negative values.
Without negative value, the correction would be under estimated and the result worse than your perfect curve (you will get waves).

You always have insulin in your body, even with negative iob (just take a look on absolute iob that is always >0).
Negative IOB signify lack of insulin compare to your basal profile.

The negative IOB is always the consequence of something else that is not correct (basal rate too high in your profile, sport, ...) and most of the time an hypo TT is the good way to correct the situation without cheating aaps.

_Another theoretical example (which I happen to experience regularly):_ 

AAPS tries to keep my BG at target using the **perfect profile**.
Then my IC is a bit off (due to todays sensitivity) and maybe I was unable to calculate carbs absorbed exactly:

AAPS/0Ref will attempt to compensate for this and keeping me at target (as designed)  by some 0-temping, 
It does so perfectly, no problems until .... negative -IOB gets me in a hypo.

_To clarify (its what i see happing when it occurs):_
Negative -IOB results into an instable system that starts cycling between lows and -IOB about every 2-3 hours:
```
|---> Going below target -> 0-temp -> going to target with -IOB -> addtional insulin for -IOB -->--|
^------------------<-------------------------------------------------------------------------<-----|
```
I can only break this cycle by taking carbs to get 2 points above target (target=5.0)

* TT does not work here: it only worsens by generating more -IOB
* Temporary loweri

> You always have insulin in your body, even with negative iob (just take a look on absolute iob that is always >0).
> Negative IOB signify lack of insulin compare to your basal profile.

That is just the point with -IOB. It is just a trick to calculate "virual" insulin that was expected but not administered.
It most certainly can be taken in account for oRef calculation. 
But it should *not* be compensated for by actually injecting this "virtual" insulin just to get to absolute insulin at "0"

There should not be any need for "tricks", T-Temps or "Basal rate lowering" to prevent something like oRef negative -IOB from causing problems. 

Even after 2 years on the subject -IOB I have not seen any (acceptable) explanation on the purpose of compensating for -IOB with real insulin

I think you have to separate two things: Showing an insulin level below the actual basal level. This is where negative IOB makes sense and is very helpful information. Negative insulin (understood as a deviation from what the basal rate would have given) must exist and must be possible and must be enabled by the algorithm. This is a binse.

The "enforced" filling of the negative IOB as soon as an opportunity comes up (positive trend, calculator ...) has no logic in my eyes. Because the available insulin quantity (even if it is IOB negative), is exactly correct at this time and was also exactly so initially controlled by the algorithm! So why correct this "correct" amount of insulin on occasion incorrectly? ;-)
This is exactly why I have to set up automations, set Hypo-TT etc., in order to moderate this, in my eyes, usually not reasonable amount of insulin.

And more fundamentally: I hope that AAPS will soon say goodbye to OREF and become independent.  There is so much developer po

threads.text:
Negative IOB : shouldn't be used in insulin calculations   There is a security risk with negative IOB. AAPS  always tries to inject the "missing" insulin which results in lows.

There is no "negative" IOB in our bodies. The pancreas releases or not insulin depending on BGs and their variations. It should be the same in AAPS.

Negative IOB is an important information for the user (ie profile too strong) and should be indicated (message and text on the graphic) but should NOT enter in the formulas used to calculate the insulin amount to be injected.

2 examples. This morning, my BGs were lower than usual (insulin working better than other mornings). AAPS does a great job and stops basal to prevent hypos. This generates negative IOB. I'm below target, no carbs. If I use the calculator, the negative IOB will be injected and I'll find myself in hypo. The calculator should not inject the negative IOB. Even without the calculator, AAPS should not try to fill in the "missing" insulin.

threads.text:
Omnipod EROS: There is no way to forcefully wipe/reset the pod state in case of "emergency"  **AAPS version 3.0.0.1 release and higher**
**Driver: Omnipod EROS**

**Problem description:**
The Omnipod EROS driver has a bug that can lead to a situation where users get stuck with a pod registration that can not be continued or discarded. Several users reported running into this problem as a result of Pod activation failure.

Work around used for not losing Objectives is importing 3.0 settings in AAPS version 2.8.1, discard the Pod and then export preferences that can be imported by AAPS 3.0

**Proposed work around**:
Until the actual bug is solved, but also in general, I think the EROS driver should have a way to "wipe" the Pod state in case of "emergencies". Up to AAPS version 2.8 this could be done by editing the unencrypted preference file.
As of version 3.0 this is no longer an option.

How about an option to clear Pod state when running in developer mode? This way users have an "escape" option to get out of situations where there is Pod state without option to Discard. For AAPS 2.8 editing the preference file was used as a last resort

 Alternative "_solution_" to the problem would be resetting AAPS preferences or a reinstall.
An option to import "objectives only" would then ensure objectives are not lost

See https://github.com/nightscout/AndroidAPS/issues/1852
 Remark:
Omnipod DASH implementation ensures that after 3 unsuccesfull retries user is offered the option to "forcefully" discarding the Pod.

Something like this maybe could also be implemented for EROS but expect this would need non-trivial driver changes?
Expecting forcefully wiping pod state from developer mode can be done with less impact on drive code?
 what keys do you have to remove? > what keys do you have to remove?

@MilosKozak 
Clearing string value at `content: "AAPS.Omnipod.pod_state"` should effectively remove the Pod on settings import.

Currently not using EROS so unable to validate. Do have 3 EROS pods reserved for dev, so can test when needed.
 FYI: Apart from settings, some hints to implementation:

Think PodState is accessible at `java/info/nightscout/androidaps/plugins/pump/omnipod/eros/manager/AapsErosPodStateManager.java`
See public methods `store/loadPodState()`

Also see also `OmnipodManager, deactivatePod()` at `java/info/nightscout/androidaps/plugins/pump/omnipod/eros/driver/manager/OmnipodManager.java`
It calls `podStateManager.discardState();` at line 504

Note that when discarding state, any active Pod is lost.
As is now, user can restore state through importing settings exported for the active Pod. Importing state from settings is useful when uninstalling/reinstalling AAPS or (unsupported) moving AAPS to other hardware.



 ![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/45144129/175774087-fb073756-327e-4c3c-a0f1-c7a3f23de5d6.png)
 Discard pod is not enough in this state?
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/11146458/175776063-bcef7f62-a862-417b-8a58-1a5aadc2d850.png)
This create empty pod state, only address is preserved Yes, the deactivation button normally should be used to solve a problematic pod.....

The bug/problem however is that AAPS/EROS somehow gets in a state where activation unexpectedly failed and activation process can not be continued. In that state however both the "Deactivate Pod" and "Discard Pod" buttons are disabled/invisible.

Not sure but I think the "Discard" button is only visible after failing to deactivate.
 Most obvious solution would be to target this specific bug (proper error handling?). But that would mean touching driver code which you may not want at this stage?

Also in any other situation, there is still no ways to repair by wiping state ....

At the moment, we've just been setting a temp target all the time to get this to work somewhat like we're wanting. It's not perfect, we'd really love to use autosens to adjust the target on the fly and to not have to remember to reset the target after activity or hypo, but it's been amazing for helping us out when we inevitably forget to indicate carbs for a meal or snack.

I just wanted to follow up on this a month later. 

We've continued setting a temp target to get something close to UAMs, and we have been *much* more lax in putting in carbs (I'd say about 50% of the time we put them in before we start to eat, 30% we put them in within 20 minutes of eating, and the rest we forget for more than 20 minutes or don't remember at all). I ran a CGP report before we started doing this, and ran one just now for the duration we've been doing this, and the numbers are a bit worse now but still surprisingly close to "We're completely on top of T1D every day because we're focusing". We're happy to share the reports if it would provide any useful information on the effectiveness of the Libre Freestyle 2 as a UAM compatible CGM.

In light of the now well-documented good performance of the freestyle Libre 3 I would love to be able to use features like autosens, UAM etc. 
I had absolutely zero issues with wrong or jumpy data. 
FL3 seems to now have a similar error correction as the dexcom sensors. Suspicious values are not sent to the phone. In such cases the sensor takes a few minutes time out. 

Here are two studies. One comparing dexcom G7 and Freestyle Libre 3. 

https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38189290/

https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC10064376/

Agreed with the comments regarding SMB-always for the Libre above. AAPS is renowned for its openness of operation and fine customisable options by the user.

User acceptance of the risks involved is an obligatory feature of building your own app, yet disabling a particular feature flies in the face of this ethos.

I don't even want to use SMB-always because I quite like the 'relaxed' operation of AAPS overnight when SMBs are off.

But to tell me I can't enable a feature stinks a bit, in my opinion.
Agree with smb always for fsl2. Already using it with a workaround with temp tarheta. Would love to use it normally

The Libre 1 bug that was reported a very long time ago, wasn’t probably even a Libre issue, but caused by the the Bluetooth interface placed on top of it. 
The issue is long gone with Libre 2.

I'm in the same boat. AAPS denies "SMB always" and "after carbs".
Using Libre 3 with Juggluco and xdrip+ my personal libre data seems to be pretty stable so i would vote for a removal of these constraints for current Libre sensors, too.

The constraints even seem to make little sense as you can easily overrule them by setting temp targets... (not tested, only read here and on discord)

UAM SMBs with Libre 2 enhancement for_discussion This is a feature/enhancement request regarding the usage of SMBs with the Libre 2 (and potentially 3).

We started objective 9 and it seems that many of the SMB options (Enable SMB Always, Enable SMB After Carbs, and, most importantly for us, Enable UAM) are unavailable to users of the Libre 2 CGM. The listed reason in the docs is a need for data smoothing as the sensors themselves do not smooth output, but we enabled a smoothing algorithm through xDrip and still cannot use these options.

We asked about the SMB options in AAPS in the WANW Discord and were informed that the L1 had a bug that might report a flat high BG during an error event instead of reporting the error, and this was the actual reason that these SMB options were disabled for the Libre 2 and 3. A discussion ensued with various people agreeing that a flat high BG is not an issue, us included- we have only ever seen a flat low BG, and even that only once in the last year.

With both of these problems (BG noise and high BG instead of error events) not being an issue for the Libre 2 and 3, and given that the Libre sensors are approved by various agencies for use in loops, we're requesting that these limitations on SMBs be lifted, potentially with enforcement of smoothing algorithm usage. comments.body: Do you also have AAPS installed on this phone ? If yes, you need to compile AAPSClient yourself, because you can't have both compiled with different keystore.

@emilisev I do have AAPS on my phone but that was always the case and previous versions of AAPSClient worked. As a matter of fact any  AAPSClient version prior to 3.3 (i.e 3.2.0.4) installs with no problem and that's what I'm using now.
Yes that's a new restriction starting from this version

I'm sorry, but I don't understand the logic behind this change. Why should my personal AAPS be linked to AAPSClient, which is solely used to monitor my daughter's sugar levels?
Especially given that AAPSClient, unlike AAPS, can be downloaded directly and doesn't require compiling from scratch.

Check the doc if you don't believe me 😉 : https://androidaps.readthedocs.io/en/latest/RemoteFeatures/RemoteControl.html#download-and-installation

I believe it is not a decision from aaps team but some limitation induced but the android libraries used (they were updated in last version).

I believe you, but I just don't understand the logic behind this change, especially since it works perfectly in version 3.2.0.4. If this change was imposed by Android libraries rather than the AAPSClient developers, then it's a different matter and beyond our control. I just want to make sure that this is indeed the case.
I guess it has something to do with 2 aaps from the same author but different keystore, since the keystore is used to authenticate the app, but I'm no specialist
The question is what has changed between AAPSClient 3.2.0.4 (everything works fine) vs 3.3 and up (won't install due to conflict).
Aaps uses a lot of android librairies, and a lot of them were updated (hence the requirement for Android 11 as well), I guess that's where it comes from.
it's android limitation. Apps that use the same permission must be signed with the same key. Permission is new in 3.3 to allow sending data to watch from multiple sources

threads.title: No Pod activation possible since Android 16 Update

comments.body:
Adding my findings. 

My phone is a Pixel 7 Pro. Running Android 15 until today with no issues on the Dash pods. I was never using the Dash bond setting.

Today I updated to Android 16, and the current pod continued to work with no settings change in AAPS.

Then I deactivated the current pod and tried to activate a new pod. The pod fails to activate with the following error:  "Failed to connect to pod"

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/466797e2-4f4a-4020-9fee-8da4acd12a51)

The logcat shows the following:

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/000be122-a991-45a1-8f80-37a69b8d3c91)

It fails waiting for the connection here:

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6ec5eba5-c57d-4754-915b-22e2647f1e0d)

This is so weird, because the same function call is used for active pods, so why was it working earlier in the day for me, but now is failing with a new pod? I also tried bonding the pod manually in the android settings and it still fails to co

Trying to experiment with your main diabetes phone is foolish thing... And upgrading to unsupported system is very foolish thing... There have been a lot of reports of different drivers/pumps not working with Android 15, and you go and upgrade to system (Android 16), that is even less supported...

Thanks @nickb24 workarount also works for me.
nice find.

short night so this will not happen again

thanks to the team for finding a solution that quick
hopefully there will be a dev version or a release soon

I would say that is by design... Closing AAPS shouldn't cancel the bolus, unless user presses the button... 

Now... Good question... Why did you do the "Close All" while bolus was executing... You need to wait until all commands are executed and then you can close your AAPS... 

That small thing there is just showing that command is executed. You can cancel command only while you are in original AAPS instance and when command was issued... AND this is especially true if you are using pump which has no other way of cancelling command (pod pumps without screen and buttons).

threads.title: AAPS+Nightscout for selfhosting (SSL)

comments.body: Have you tried Lets encrypt. Open a basic webserver for auth then copy the key over to your private NS front end proxy or NS server directly.

Hi @Tornado-Tim, thanks for the follow-up. I am using NS from docker, and I allow access to my docker containers through Caddy with my domain. Caddy provides https by default with Let's Encrypt. My issue is that even if I have https+domain+NS, whoever knows the address (whichever robot scans the web), the NS page is accessible to the world. 

Now, Caddy provides a basic auth solution: https://caddyserver.com/docs/caddyfile/directives/basicauth. Do you refer to this option? Do you think that the API secret can go through this authentication regardless?
In that case, you can use a certbot for wildcard cert and DNS auth which will allow you to get your certs for NS. Since its wildcard, your NS will not need to be exposed.

Yeah, this might work. Unfortunately I have a domain with GoDaddy, and the DNS auth module is not ready yet (no experience with the Go language, so I cannot write one myself). I was wondering, will AndroidAPS accept self-signed certificates? Or it must be from signed by entities like LE?
i'm not familiar with caddy but nginx has `allow` and `deny` directives for access filtering
When you like use a selfhosted webservice NS with private selfsigned certificate, you must import the public key in android trust store. See android setting in security selection.

Yeah, these are all way too complex solutions compared to the single and simple one: there should be a login page for NS, after entering the credentials it should allow the user to the next page. Contacting the API with the API_SECRET is fine, I am not sure how it works in the background, and whether it should happen on another port once opened to the Internet. 

By this simple solution one can then expose the NS server with a reverse proxy solution - with https.

I have a similar problem. AAPS can receive and send encrypted data to my selfhosted nightscout-docker, but AAPS cannot retain the connection. Instead of the "ping" I get an XHR poll error ... I have a Let's encrypt certificate for this subdomain and use a reverse proxy.

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/11146458/99902026-1bb0a500-2cbb-11eb-95a2-95aba4e909fb.png)
this is my nginx setting

OK, I made it working with the latest NS version (I used niepi/cgm-remote-monitor:14.0.7), there one needs to authenticate even for viewing the web frontend. With this I was able to open the site to the Internet.

FYI, I use Caddy for securing the web with https by default (I have a domain), if this helps, I am pasting the `Caddyfile` config, which is super simple:

```
ns.{$MY_DOMAIN} {
   reverse_proxy 192.168.0.40:1337
}
```

threads.title: Can't calibrate new g6 + new transmitter: "invalid impossible slope"

comments.body: Just tried the latest nightly.  Same issue.
What firmware version does your new G6 transmitter report in System Status?

Hey jamorham, 

Having same issue. If I am correct that this is the firmware version, it is 14a03a7-2019.05.18. In case it helps, the code is 1905181006 and downgradeable to: 1603091400.

Same issue as OP. For note, I purchased this transmitter at Costco and the body appears a bit different than the others I have gotten in past. Is G6, for clarity. The transmitter SN is 8GDNQB.

Guys: for 8Gxxx transmitters you need to use at least the current Alpha version as the newer firmware is somewhat different. I would say use the Nightly version to be sure you have the most up to date support for it.

You also need to use ob1 collector in native mode so there should be no calibration involved.

Hey jamorham,

Thanks for the fast response. I would talk endlessly about the difference this app makes it my life, save for fear of it seeming trite in this medium. 

I am running nightly build from 9.10.19 and am using OB1 in native mode. As for calibration, I am showing a straight line 98 in the app, but multiple finger pricks are 78, 76 and 81, respectively.

@jamorham my firmware version is 2.18.2.88.  SN 8GFR1G, Calibration code 5937.

Still seeing this with 0e3b27181-2019.09.10, 3 which is the lately nightly available on github (from 2 days ago).   Using ob1.  Enabling/disabling the fallback doesn't seem to help.

A few additional observations:

* Initial calibration still seems to actually work.  The problem is the result intepretation, and xdrip thinking that it hasn't worked.  So it stays in initial calibration state, and keeps prompting.

* None of the following work, probably just due to the "initial calibration required" state:

* Entering a normal calibration in xdrip
* Choosing calibrate from a pre-existing BG sample point (point remains a square, rather than becoming a circle)
* Entering a calibration from AAPS.
Same issue here. Like @lee-b said, seems like that the calibrations are working fine but xDrip thinks that they got deleted - at least that's what the `Events Log` tells me.

I think xdrip is purposefully deleting them as invalid, because it misinterprets the results from the G6 transmitter, and thinks that the calibration was rejected as invalid by the G6 transmitter.

i.e., the real problem seems to be that XDrip doesn't yet know how to handle the new G6 transmitter protocol's calibration method, or its calibration response code changes.
Just changed my son's transmitter. It is serial number 81A***. Same issue. Tried alpha release and nightly release with no effect. Firmware version 1.6.5.25. Xdrip version 7d97b62-2019.09.30.

threads.title: Google Pixel 3a, Dexcom G5

comments.body:
Not exactly sure what fixed it, but it's working now on my Pixel 3a.

Things I did:
1. Disabled collection in xdrip.
2. Installed Dexcom G5 Mobile app (modified version that allows use on unsupported devices), restarted phone, and wasn't able to get the transmitter working with the dexcom app either.
3. Changed the device name of my phone's Bluetooth to something shorter, without spaces, apostrophes, etc.
4. Restarted phone again.  Dexcom G5 app started to be able to communicate with transmitter.
5. Uninstalled Dexcom G5, re-enabled G5 collection in xdrip. xdrip was now able to communicate with the transmitter.

Having the exact same issue on my Pixel 3a XL ever since changing the sensor yesterday; no Bluetooth connection and seeing "No valid timestamp stored for transmitter".  

Still not working after changing the phone / BT name.

I ran into the issue again after closing this issue, but fumbling for a bit was able to clear it up.  Still not exactly sure what fixed it as my "fix" was more analogous to a monkey pounding on the keyboard, doing most of this with my BG hovering around 40-60 mg/dL .  (Love xdrip, but its UI does require way too much cognitive load for me in that state.)

Probably the most relevant things I did while flailing about:
1. Set scan for G5 constantly.
2. Removed any G5 pairings in the phone's Bluetooth settings.
3. Restarted phone. (both restart, and power off, power on.)
4. Opened up the phone's bluetooth pairing screen and Xdrip in split screen mode.  Keeping the phone awake, waited for the G5 to pop up on the phone's Bluetooth list (didn't pair it there), and hit "RESTART COLLECTOR" in Xdrip's "Classic Status Page", then switched to "G5/G6 Status" and waited for a successful connection.  (Probably did 3 & 4 a half dozen times before it started to work again.)

Been working for ab

Glad it's working for you!

In an effort to troubleshoot I tried going back to the G6 receiver... It also couldn't find or pair with the transmitter.

So I'm assuming the transmitter is defective, just spoke to Dexcom support and they are sending a replacement.

Google Pixel 3a, Dexcom G5  Anyone have any luck with xDrip on a Google Pixel 3a running android 10 connecting to Dexcom G5?

My logs show continuous "No valid timestamp stored for transmitter: 41U5BR", and Classic Status Page says "Bluetooth Device: None Set".  Was working with a Moto G6 before. Not exactly sure what fixed it, but it's working now on my Pixel 3a.

Things I did:
1. Disabled collection in xdrip.
2. Installed Dexcom G5 Mobile app (modified version that allows use on unsupported devices), restarted phone, and wasn't able to get the transmitter working with the dexcom app either.
3. Changed the device name of my phone's Bluetooth to something shorter, without spaces, apostrophes, etc.
4. Restarted phone again.  Dexcom G5 app started to be able to communicate with transmitter.
5. Uninstalled Dexcom G5, re-enabled G5 collection in xdrip. xdrip was now able to communicate with the transmitter.
 Having the exact same issue on my Pixel 3a XL ever since changing the sensor yesterday; no Bluetooth connection and seeing "No valid timestamp stored for transmitter".  

Still not working after changing the phone / BT name. I ran into the issue again after closing this issue, but fumbling for a bit was able to clear it up.  Still not exactly sure what fixed it as my "fix" was more analogous to a monkey pounding on the keyboard, doing most of this with my BG hovering around 40-60 mg/dL .  (Love xdrip, but its UI does require way too much cognitive load for me in that state.)

Probably the most relevant things I did while flailing about:
1. Set scan for G5 constantly.
2. Removed any G5 pairings in the phone's Bluetooth settings.
3. Restarted phone. (both restart, and power off, power on.)
4. Opened up the phone's bluetooth pairing screen and Xdrip in split screen mode.  Keeping the phone awake, waited for the G5 to pop up on the phone's Bluetooth list (didn't pair it there), and hit "RESTART COLLECTOR" in Xdrip's "Classic Status Page", then switched to "G5/G6 Status" and waited for a successful connection.  (Probably did 3 & 4 a half dozen times before it started to work again.)

Been working for ab Glad it's working for you!

In an effort to troubleshoot I tried going back to the G6 receiver... It also couldn't find or pair with the transmitter.

So I'm assuming the transmitter is defective, just spoke to Dexcom support and they are sending a replacement.

2) Choose libre as the sensor type.

6) Start a new sensor (answer not today).
7) Go to settings->less common settings->other misc options-> and set "use
oop algorithm"

This configuration is far from being intuitive, but users will see the BG
and alerts will work and so on.

comments.body: I've been having the same issue, but I think it's only when I enter a calibration code of 0000 (e.g. when I restart a sensor). Is that the same for you?

Thanks for the feedback but clear "NO" - I am always entering the calibration code, see in screenshot below (here 7171). Do you see the "Initial Calibration" menu item? In my case it's always there and this is the only way for me to enter calibrations. Anybody else having this issue?

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/60714349/79902358-a83b7200-8411-11ea-915b-a6335eebf08c.png)

Yes, I do have the "Initial Calibration" item in the menu, and it is the only way I can currently calibrate. I also get the exact same errors that you're describing. I had this issue previously and a complete wipe and re-install of xDrip fixed it. However, I ended up back in the same scenario, but I haven't yet identified the specific trigger. I assumed it was the sensor restart, but it appears that's not the case. I'll let you know if it goes back to normal after starting a new sensor (probably within a couple days). If not, I'll wipe and pay more attention as I configure things to see if I can pinpoint the trigger. Some more details about my config: - Original Pixel, running Android 10 - xDrip version: d0011d1-2020.03.25 - Data Source: G6 Native - Status page: - G5/G6 Settings

I also do sensor restarts (stop session, pop out, wait 15min, pop back in => start session). When re-starting I always enter the initial calibration code (never used 0000 before). My G5/G6 debug settings differ in some switches (see my config above). So all of that's is probably not the trigger...

I have done frequent xDrip updates by downloading a more recent nightly or by using the auto-update function. Currently we're both using the same version 03/25 - we could upgrade to the latest alpha from April 19th but probably this does not fix our problem - I'm monitoring the changelog and saw no hint these updates solve our problem.

Maybe @jamorham or any other specialist can have a look and give us a good hint. I'm sure we're not the only ones...

Just documenting some troubleshooting. I started a new sensor with the calibration code. After warmup, I get the same rejection errors and see the Initial Calibration option in the hamburger menu. I backed up my settings, uninstalled xDrip, reinstalled, and restored the settings. I ignored all prompts to start the sensor (since it was already started). Once connected again, I was in the same situation. Next, I stopped the sensor, uninstalled xDrip, popped out the transmitter, reinstalled, and did **not** restore settings. Followed setup and wizard as if setting up for the first time. I'll report back with my findings once warmup is done and I'm awake.

Unfortunately, no luck. In addition to the steps mentioned above, I
-  Started the sensor using the https://github.com/NightscoutFoundation/xDrip/commit/8c4987f16f5481f73ecdbe62de2c26cc7fe7d218 version (buddy said it was working for him)
- Started the sensor using Dexcom's app before switching to xDrip

neither of which fixed the issue.

Next, I'm going to dive into the code to investigate the specific errors to see if I can figure anything out from that perspective.

I have good news to help get functional again! I downgraded to the [2019.10.27 Nightly Build](https://github.com/NightscoutFoundation/xDrip/releases/tag/2019.10.27) and calibration seems to work now. I had an issue with Bluetooth dropping communication, but I think it was because I had a permission set incorrectly. I'm not giving up on digging in deeper, but I just needed something stable to fall back to for own psychological well-being. @emp-00, hopefully this will help you as well!

The G5/G6 settings I currently have toggled **on** for this version:
- Use the OB1 Collector
- Native Algorithm
- Go on without calibrations
- G6 Support
- Allow OB1 unbonding
- Allow OB1 initiate bonding
- Authenticate G5 before each read

@emp-00, following up on your message...

I doubt it's a wrong phone setting since I haven't changed anything in my phone other than downgrading the version of xDrip. I'm curious, did you happen to start a transmitter in a different timezone? Though, I don

Oh, another thing to note is that the Initial Calibration section of the hamburger menu is still there in my current working configuration, so it's presence is not sufficient to claim that the ideal calibration approach is not working.

Instead of checking that menu, I've been monitoring the G5/G6 status tab to ensure that a single calibration is queued immediately after an attempt to calibrate, and then confirming that the calibration was transmitted and accepted by the transmitter by viewing the Events Log. Note that when using the "Initial Calibration" menu item, it queues two calibrations even if only one is entered, but the ideal calibration approach only queues one.

Thanks justinthomas for your efforts! That's encouraging! 

I have JUST restarted my tx after another 10 days: first reading +100 mg/dL too high (as "always") and calibrated down by -20% with the Initial Calibration function. As you mentioned always (2) calibrations are queued with this method, confirmed. Tx accepted this first calibration! Damn I'm LUCKY :-) !! The last time I did this I had to restart once more due to "confused calibration" messages. Does anybody know if 20% or a fixed -XX mg/dL is the limit which makes the tx accept calibrations? And how long must I wait until the next calibrations step can be entered without crash?

Now I JUST saw your posting. I have to wait now for 1 or better 2 hours (anbody knows better?) before the next calibration (I'm still almost 50 mg/dL off). Then I will try the syringe again. Have changed my settings as per your suggestion above (switched these 2 ON: "Go on without Calibrations" and "Authenticate G5 before each..."). Maybe this is do

comments.body: Should be the same, both use the data from the freestyle libre sensor 2 itself. With the patched app you dont need an extra device, that already made my decision for the patched app. In my oppinion miaomiao is only helpfluu if you use libre 1 sensors. Perhaps if you are a looper (having a automated pump aswell) the miaomiao can have advanteges, but i dont do that thats why i cant tell.
But I thought that the patched app gave you the processed values by Abbott, and MiaoMiao just the raw values. Isn't that true?
Both (miamia and libre) use a routine to handle the raw data. Im not 100% sure about the miaomiao algorithm and didnt found a comparison between both, but i guess the libre one is tested a lot :)

Hi,
I've just received my first FreeStyle Libre 2 sensor (until yesterday I was using Libre 1). I was very happy with my Miao Miao 2 and Xdrip, but now I found that is not working anymore (I get the "Checksum failed" error everytime, there's no way to make it works).
Then, you guys wrote above that we don't need the Miao Miao 2 anymore, we can use the LibreLink app patched with xDrip+??? is there any guide to do that? where/how can I find the patched app??
Thank you!

@jomonba1 read this guide. at the bottom its in englisch:
https://github.com/TinoKossmann/LibreLink-xDrip-Patch
If you read this here is another guide for how to youse xdrip in combination with the patched libre app
https://androidaps.readthedocs.io/en/latest/EN/Configuration/xdrip.html#xdrip-freestyle-libre (you can change the language on the left side of the page)

Having used both setups as well as MM1 and Libre 1 before, I am now confidently using Libre2 with only the patched app.  

Recently I was calibrating the Libre2 in XDrip+ and I have now stopped that completely.  Reason being is that calibrations were always throwing off the values.  I get that the slope calibration should provide a better approximation but in my experience it was not working well.   I did all the right things, wait until BG is stable, do a sensor change, no carbs for 3 hours prior, low stress during calibration, initial calibration of 2 BG tests.   Then the next few days I would do a calibration when I woke up as BG was stable from during the previous night.   

A user on Gitter (twinko, I think) mentioned that they were not using calibrations with Libre2, this peaked my interest so I set aside 2 weeks to try this.   Here is what I found.

**Goal:**  Minimalist

threads.title: Android 10+ asks every 5 minutes for pairing with Dexcom transmitter

comments.body:
After upgrade to oct 2020 android samsung a50 every 5 minutes xdrip 2020 asks for dexcom bluetooth connection when syncing. If you do not agree with the request to connect the dexcom bluetooth sensor, xdrip sync does not work.
The xdrip app released in 2019 works fine. Synchronization of the smartphone and dexcom takes place without a request.
How to remove the request to connect dexcom via bluetooth on the a50 smartphone on xdrip later edition of xdrip?

I am experiencing what I believe may be the same issue. xDrip making a bluetooth pairing request for the Dexcom 
transmitter every couple of minutes. It is extremely annoying and frustrating.

This is on a Samsung Galaxy S10 and started happening with the last phone update yesterday.

Galaxy S10 (SM-G973U1)
Build Number : G973U1UES4ETJ3
Android version : Q(Android 10)
Release Date : 2020-11-02
Security patch level : 2020-11-01

2020.07.13 e14bae1

Have not been able to work around this :(

![20201103_221738](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/59528752/98065513-c18e9380-1e22-11eb-976f-20032d0a120b.jpg)

@BKrueckeberg Can you confirm that the nightly from [May 18, 2019](https://github.com/NightscoutFoundation/xDrip/releases/tag/2019.05.18) works for you?

@vitalykekukh Please help us by finding the latest version which works for you.

now this version works well

https://github.com/NightscoutFoundation/xDrip/releases/tag/2019.05.18

@vitalykekukh Now, I'm confused. What is the difference between the latest comments with respect to the release tag? Please can you remove redundant comments and just edit a (potentially) wrong comment?

@vitalykekukh I cannot believe that [2019.05.18](https://github.com/NightscoutFoundation/xDrip/releases/tag/2019.05.18) is the latest version which works because there are only Libre-related changes in [2019.05.19](https://github.com/NightscoutFoundation/xDrip/releases/tag/2019.05.19), for instance. It would be really helpful to find the latest tagged version which works for you. Please can you try newer versions of every month after May, 2019 until you found a breaking version and than go stepwise back the tags?
I am having the same issue on my Pixel 5. I tried the May 19 version but the same thing happened

I tried the [2019.05.18](https://github.com/NightscoutFoundation/xDrip/releases/tag/2019.05.18) build on my Samsung Galaxy S10. 

I am NOT experiencing the ongoing Bluetooth pairing requests anymore BUT am also loosing transmitter connection after only a handful of successfully received signals. I am seeing 'Aggressively restarting collector service due to lack of reception backoff' being logged every couple of minutes.

Bottom line is that the [2019.05.18](https://github.com/NightscoutFoundation/xDrip/releases/tag/2019.05.18) doesn't work. Please let me know how I can support you in figuring out a solution!

Thanks

The difference between the old and new versions of Android is the enhanced Bluetooth security system. The developers claim that hackers can steal data from a smartphone via Bluetooth. So in the new version of Android, they have enabled an additional pairing request. 
The 2019 version of xdrip is permanently paired via Bluetooth. To save battery power, the 2020 versions connect via Bluetooth every 5 minutes and then disconnect. Therefore, when paired, Android recognizes the pairing as connecting a new device and issues a request to the smartphone user. In this situation, either the xdrip developers in the new versions will make permanent pairing via Bluetooth, or the Android developers will make it possible to make a one-time request to pair with a known (allowed) device.

Thanks for the explanation @vitalykekukh. That would make sense based on what I am experiencing with my phone. 

Do you happen to know with what version this power save feature was added exactly? I have tried the 2019.05.18 version but this hasn't worked well for me either (due to other issues).

xDrip confuses G5 with a G6 and performs a preemptive restart on day 9 as well as on day 6 bug device-dexcom calibration device-dexcom-transmitter ### Expected behavior
Dexcom G5 can be used in Native mode.  But, since G5 sends raw data, you can still access the calibration graph.  And xDrip removes "Initial calibration" from the menu after initial calibrations have been submitted and replaces it with "Add calibration".

### Your environment
The problem was observed with the February 11, 2021 release, and February 3, 2021.


### Actual behavior
Calibrations are sent to the transmitter and are accepted by the G5 transmitter.  However, xDrip logs show they are rejected by xDrip.
![tempFileForShare_20210216-234941](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/51497406/108206590-96d7fa80-70f4-11eb-93a3-64454447f949.jpg)

Logs show calibrations have been rejected.
No access to adding calibration in the top left menu as only initial calibration is shown there.
No access to calibration graph.
Empty calibration data table.

The symptoms match the behavior of xDrip with a device that does not send raw data like a Firefly G6,

After installing the January 29, 2021 version, the problem was resolved. 


### Steps to reproduce the behavior:
Install xDrip release February 11, 2021
Start a G5 sensor in native mode
Apply initial calibrations
Check calibration data table, or check the logs.

@viq:hackerspace.pl reported this in the Gitter room.
Another individual reported it on facebook where the calibration graph being missing and the calibration data table being empty were reported.

comments.body:
When I last looked at it, google removed the possibility to add text there (at least for non-system apps) - and also the possibility to add dynamically rendered icons. Too many apps where pushing advertisement there, without the possibility for the user to know what app it was :/
Newer versions of Android might get (have gotten) the possibility to do that again?

What apps then usually did was exchanging the icon. Having a range from 40 to 400, this would mean more than 360 icons for mg/dl alone. Additionally those for mmol/l.
Even if it is possible to dynamically render the icon I believe its going to be limited to a tiny space and getting 3 digits in there is going to pretty difficult and for it to be readable.
What about some sort of middle ground... perhaps three or four icons:  red:  low, green:  in range, yellow: high... or some such thing.

Great to see that my suggetion receives attention.Thanks for this!

Im running the Pixel 2 XL with Android Oreo. Im not sure how AccuBattery implements this feature as im not really an expert in that regard...


Perhaps ill photoshop a mockup to see if 3 digits would be feasible. But Im hopeful that it would fit the space as accubattery uses 2 digits + the circle.

The color solution depends on the android version youre running. From my experience Android Oreo converts every notification with colored icons to b/w.

Well... I guess the takeaway here is that "more information is better".  Currently the status bar icon of a static xdrip symbol brings very little to no "information" value.  There are certainly tons of apps, such as this weather app I use that successfully show dynamic info in that space... such as the current temp (which in "f" can range from -xx to +xxx temps).  So, it certainly is possible.  The heartache seems to be on the implementation side... all the work to make icons with each BG value.  So, the bottom line is... is the value gained by having a dynamic status bar icon greater than the work involved?  I'd certainly volunteer my time in the grunt work of creating those BG png files.  We'd be looking at what... Maybe an "L" symbol for 40 and lower... then 41 -> 300 or so?  Then an "H" for high?

Ok, I think I have a lot of stuff working now. I'm getting data from the sensor. We have the option to use the A6 native algorithm or the xDrip algorithm. 

I'm going to make it an option which to show as the primary number and then plot the alternate algorithm as a trace behind it so we can work out which may be the most useful. There may need some tuning to work properly with xDrip calibration algorithm which as a lot of dex style assumptions in it.

Okay the July 19th nightly contains support for the Medtrum A6. Its about 2000+ lines of code so far!

To get it to work you should select Medtrum A6 in the hardware data source settings section. Then use `Bluetooth Scan` to identify the A6 transmitter. It isn't always discoverable so you often have to keep clicking scan until it shows up. If its not attached to your body then pop it in the charging doc and after a few seconds it should be visible. threads.title: Improve support for Finowatch / Finow Q1 PRO

comments.body:
As a collector of miaomiao this works well.
The q1 pro itself is a very low end watch. Battery might last from 7 hours to 18 hours with no good reason.
keyboard is almost useless. screen is low quality. (I guess that this is what you can get for 75 usd).
That said,  I'm not aware of issues as a collector.

I used the watch Finow Q1 Pro with G5 as a collector in old mode, trying almost all versions of xDrip+ starting from August this year. The readings were received with intervals of 5 minutes and were transmitted to the Nightscout by the watch through 3G. But there was no stability, packet capture percentage was about 50-70 %. The collector used to terminate work when the charge was below 30 %. Ticked wakelocks and watchdogs could not prevent failure in operation. I think it depends on the in-build algorithm of energy saving. The battery life was 8-10 hours, Wi-Fi was disabled, BT and 3G were enabled, brightness was at the lowest level, and I made just a couple of messages (or calls).
Also I tried to use this watch as a collector in OB1 mode (including Native Algorithm). The readings were received with intervals of 10 minutes and were transmitted to the Nightscout by the watch through 3G. This interval was inacceptable for me, so I left this mode.

My daughter use Finow Q1 Pro with G5(FW. 1.0.4.10).I set up them as a collector in OB1 mode with out native mode.In G5 Debug Settings mark only Use the OB1 Collector and Allow OB1 initiate bonding. And disable all in less common settings relates to bluetooth. Install root on watch and disabled all unused apps. Packet capture percentage about 85-95%.The readings  received with intervals of 5 minutes and  transmitted to the Nightscout by the watch through 3G. 
But some time watch lose connection totally, helps only restart watch, or start receive data with intervals of 10 minutes. After 5 minutes when it no get data  I check in System Status - G5 Status - Phone Service Status it's show that it stuck on Connection request.
So I set up alarm on missing reading and just rerstart watch.
And if I start mess with in less common settings or G5 Debug Settings I get no change in connections.

gordan1987, did you manage to unlock the bootloader on the finow q1 pro watch? This question was also asked @jamorham in gitter on 18th Nov. I think he has some ideas for improving collector service of this watch. And hope he is planning to realize “wearDemiGod” mode for this watch.
I upload all for [rooting to Mega](https://mega.nz/#F!fQkiyC7L!3NhHK9DpAO6bqVApPXnncA)

I have enabled verbose longing for OB1 collector on this watch for Dexcom G6 sensor. The logs with the problematic situation as described by gordan1987 have been uploaded through xdrip with the information "#648" and my email address (lmiekus@gmail.com) The problem appeared at 23:10, since that time watch was unable to connect to the sensors. Only after restarting watch the connection have been restored . If you have any other questions please let me know. I am also attaching the exact configuration of the phone with all the important settings.
[Settings.docx](https://github.com/NightscoutFoundation/xDrip/files/2722310/Settings.docx)
It would be nice if xDrip had a possibility to restart the clock, if no data received. For me this only way to restore receiving data.

Did you thought about trying less common settings > Bluetooth settings > Timer value for BT Watchdog  set to 6 minutes and Bluetooth Watchdog checkbox ticked? I am occasionally getting lost connections as described by you, we usually do smartwatch restart to solve it. But I am planing to try this option too.  That option to set timer value is not possible in last stable version of xdrip+. I found this one in nightly from 28.12.2018.
I try set Timer value to 6 minutes in nightly. Still no luck, only restart helps.

Did someone try to run the old collector (without OB1) on this watch? On Russian diabet forum, people says that it works well with G5 transmitter. Also they say this watch works reliably with blucon and Miao-Miao (transmitters for Libre sensor).

comments.body:
Which version of ESEL do you use?
The traditional one: Did you make sure your phone is not only rooted but also has sqlite3 installed?

The new one that does not need root: Did you patch the Eversens app on your own or get the apk from somewhere?

Hey thanks for your fast response. I am using the newest Eversense XL for 7 days now. I did not know that I have to patch the Eversense App, since I did not find anything about how to set it up, so I just used the newest xDrip Apk and the latest version of Eversense CGM from the PlayStore. How can I get that patched Eversense App?

You do need the companion app "ESEL": https://github.com/AdrianLxM/Esel/

At the moment you do have to build it for yourself. As up until recently you had to be quite tech-savvy anyway (flash another operating system onto the phone) this was the way to go.

We are working on a more user-friendly option now that you don't have to root the phone anymore.

There is an easier solution availabe as well:
https://github.com/BernhardRo/Esel/tree/master/apk
This does not require a rooted phone and no compiling...

@xLevelster: Can you provide some informations regarding the system itself? How long does the battery of the transmitter last? Is it easy to remove it (for snorkeling/diving) and attach again? How accurate is it? What  happens when you don't calibrate twice a day?

Battery lasts up to 36 hours. It is very easy to remove because it is just sticked to your skin with an adhesive. For me it is super accurate. You won't get any readings after 2 hours when you don't calibrate.

Yes, the battery lasts for about 36h, but it takes only roughly 10 min to reload it. Therefore it is no problem to easily take it off every day (e.g. before taking a shower) and reload it. For me, this is even an advantage as my skin had problems with the 14 days of wearing a freestyle libre. With eversense my skin gets a break and a new plaster every day and with this I have no problems at all.
In terms of accuracy: the values are somehow noisy, but accurate.
Can you fix it without a plaster with armband or 3d printed holder?

> Can you fix it without a plaster with armband or 3d printed holder?

Yes not really necessary but that should work, depending on how good it stays over the sensor.
I ask because I have to remove it on some days more than once when I go diving...

comments.body: It sounds like the phone's bluetooth stack has problems. I don't have one of these phones to test with. If anyone can loan me one I should be able to discover more quite quickly.

The Atom BT stack is quite messed up it seems.
I also have problems keeping the BT connection up with a combo pump and with a Dana RS. So neither BLE nor older BT standards seem to work reliably.

It would be good if you could contact the tech support of unihertz. They will give you a guide how to send them system logs. I hope if they get them with different setups they will find a fix.
I don't have much hope as the December update still had the may security patch level of android :(

Hi, We are the technical support of unihertz.
As the document <log-check-20190109.pdf> describes, can Xdrip app give some instructions and why is it broken?
[log-check-20190109.pdf](https://github.com/NightscoutFoundation/xDrip/files/2739098/log-check-20190109.pdf)

Hey guys, I am currently using ATOM (latest firmware) together with xDrip (latest nightly) reading G6 and AAPS (latest dev) with Dana RS pump. It works so far (> 1-2 weeks) without the need to do regular restarts. 
When I try to add my Sony SWR50 I get BT communication problems - mostly with AAPS. 

I was in contact with Unihertz since I got the phone back in October and we have tried to identify what's amiss (I guess the log above is from mine from end of Nov) but without any success. 

I really would like to use the ATOM with my setup together with a smartwatch - this would be my idea of a perfect system for looping.

Please let me know if I can help with any testing.

I have made screenshots of my current system and app settings for your reference: https://photos.app.goo.gl/bi8axT9pnRTHBuH9A

-------------
Adrian, Unihertz says on their ATOM FB group that the patch level was updated with their latest FW but not recognized by Google. 
![image](https://user-images.githubu

@tech-support-unihertz I am the developer of the OB1G5Service. The dexcom transmitter wakes up periodically (every 5 minutes) for a short period of time and during that wake up window we need to connect to it to retrieve the data.  That is what the service is doing.

I don't have an atom device to test here in the lab but the reports from users have been that the whole phone needs to be rebooted which in my experience implies that it is quite likely the android bluetooth subsystem itself is crashing.

@jamorham Can you help analyze this log? (Thanks for the log provider @2flea  :)
https://www.dropbox.com/s/0f2cmdvxjqmt5ni/mtklog_20181127.zip?dl=0
From the log analysis, Bluetooth data interaction is normal from 21:02 to 21:38. At 21:39:38 seconds, because there is no data interaction, Bluetooth switches to IDLE mode, causing the connection to be disconnected. 
Can you tell us if the xdrip app received an error code when the problem occurred?

As far as I remember the log set above was done with the pre-release firmware including the "Bluetooth has stopped" message not the current version. Also I had different settings in the Atom battery saving. 
@tech-support-unihertz, @jamorham I can provide new log data with the current setup and then with the Sony smartwatch if you want. Let me know if should add anything special in xDrip log settings.

Hey guys, I am also currently using ATOM (latest firmware) together with xDrip (latest nightly) reading G6, and fitbit versa and have struggled to keep a connection to bluetooth when adding a smartwatch (Fitbit Versa) to the configuration.

**History:  
Test1:**  Tried atom and versa with xdrip and **Atom October firmware**. Tested every battery, fitbit, and collector setting combination imaginable with no joy.
**Result1:** Had tons of connection drops and the only way to resolve them was to reboot phone.  Happened every few hours.

**Test2:**  Updated **atom firmware to November (latest)** and tuned xdrip, fitbit,  and android settings.  Also "Forgot" Sensor in Bluetooth, and let xdrip populate a new Dexcom Bluetooth connection. Still using versa smartwatch.
**Result2:**  Seemed to stay connected a little better, but still had disconnects when the phone was out of range and brought back into range.  Many unrecoverable disconnects a day that required rebooting the phone to solve

I have received a unihertz atom phone to test with. It is early days, but my initial findings are that the problems are due to the manufacturers power saving additions to android which shut down xDrip.

`PowerSaveService: forceStopThirdApp processName: com.eveningoutpost.dexdrip  pid: 6814, packageName:com.eveningoutpost.dexdrip`

This happens even though the custom setting for the app "`Background activity`" is enabled for xDrip and that xDrip is already supposed to be excluded from battery optimization via its standard android runtime permission for the same. 

The MTK setting for `Intelligent power saving standby` is also disabled as well as `battery saver` in the general battery settings.

xDrip is running a foreground service and does not target oreo sdk (targets sdk 23)

This is running on an atom with build number `20181130`

As far as I can tell the custom setting for whether `Background activity` is allowed for a specific app either is not implemented or doesn't wo

Could someone from Unihertz please comment on what can be done to get this
fixed, so that we can use the phones and watches effectively with Bluetooth
CGM softwares?

distilled.title: Riley Link Orange can't connect with dev branch
distilled.symptom: RileyLink Orange cannot connect with dev branch; state stuck at initialization of RileyLink. No permission request notification appears. Connection works with master branch.
distilled.cause: The problem is the RL check for permission before connect code, specifically in RileyLinkBLE.kt connectGattInternal where the condition uses >= Build.VERSION_CODES.S, causing the permission request not to appear on Android 12.
distilled.fix: Change the condition in RileyLinkBLE.kt from `if (config.PUMPDRIVERS && Build.VERSION.SDK_INT >= Build.VERSION_CODES.S && ...` to `if (config.PUMPDRIVERS && Build.VERSION.SDK_INT > Build.VERSION_CODES.S && ...` to bypass the permission check and allow connection.

distilled.title: [2.7] All delta get set to 0 after 30s (Dexcom patched app and xDrip)
distilled.symptom: When using xDrip as source (with G6) the delta in homescreen is (almost always) 0 for all three deltas. The deltas get set to 0 exactly 30 seconds after the BG reading comes in. This also occurs when using the patched Dexcom app as source.
distilled.cause: The setup DEX -> AAPS -> XDRIP -> NS -> APPS causes data to be changed by xDrip in the middle of the chain, so it's not deduplicated on AAPS side, resulting in deltas of 0 for duplicate values.
distilled.fix: Disable all inter-app communication and upload settings in xDrip, and re-enable BG upload in AAPS. This stops duplicate uploads to Nightscout.
distilled.evidence_quote: Disabling all inter-app communication + upload settings in xdrip and then **re-enabling BG upload in AAPS** did the trick.

distilled.symptom: On Galaxy Watch 4, with AAPS 3.0.0, bolus progress events cause sound and vibration on the watch despite the 'Vibrate on bolus' setting being OFF. Users want to silence both sound and vibration for bolus progress.
distilled.cause: The issue is caused by the changed API for notification. Before the last Wear OS update, the notification could be changed; now it cannot be silenced easily.
distilled.fix: Workaround: Disable the AAPS notification channel 'AAPS Bolus Progress Silent' in the watch's Developer options (Settings > Developer options > App notifications > Show all > AAPS > switch off channel). Also ensure 'Vibrate on Bolus' is off in AAPS watch settings. The issue was later solved in 3.1 beta 1 by using a separate notification tile.
distilled.evidence_quote: There is a workaround, for now, disabling the notification completely: - Enable **Developer Settings** if you haven't already. - About > Software > and keep tapping on **Software Version** until a toast appears. - Back into Settings menu, **Developer options** - Scroll to bottom > App notifications > **Show all** - Select **AAPS** - Switch off the channel **AAPS Bolus Progress Silent**

distilled.title: Wrong IOB, because boluses are shown twice
distilled.symptom: In AndroidAPS 3.0, some meal-boluses and SMBs are shown twice in the treatments-tab, while the pump shows them only once, leading to incorrect (too high) IOB.
distilled.cause: The timestamp of a bolus was not adjusted to the time it was actually received by the pump; it kept the time the command was sent. This caused a mismatch when pairing with pump history, leading to duplicate entries. This behavior was lost during refactoring to Kotlin and new database code.
distilled.fix: Adjust the timestamp of the bolus entry to the time it was received on the pump (instead of the time the command was sent), so that when history is read, the bolus can be correctly paired with the pump history entry. This fix is implemented in branch bug1768_2xbolus and PR #1825.
distilled.evidence_quote: So when we do bolus on pump, before entry is written into database, timestamp is adjusted (it doesn't contain previous timestamp, when AAPS/orefx sent bolus command, but timestamp when bolus was received on pump), so when history comes back it will easily be tied to actual bolus record. This might prevent double bolus...

distilled.title: [3.1.0.3-dev-a] Calibration in BYODA -> BG too close (red triangle) -> LGS (low glucose suspend)
distilled.symptom: When doing a calibration in BYODA, a new BG is sent to AAPS close to the last one instead of updating it, causing a 'BG too close' error with a red triangle and the loop falls back to LGS (low glucose suspend).
distilled.cause: BYODA sends readings not respecting the 'every 5 minutes' rule, causing duplicate BG readings close together, which leads to incorrect delta calculations affecting algorithm performance.
distilled.fix: The issue is mostly resolved except for rare situations; resolving the rest would slow down BG processing too much. Workaround: manually delete the duplicated BG from BYODA tab of AAPS.

distilled.cause: Manual BG entries from a BG meter are uploaded as the wrong record type (CGM values instead of self-monitored BG values). The type is 'cgb' in BloodGlucoseElement.kt, but should be 'smbg'.
distilled.fix: The fix was to change the record type from 'cgb' to 'smbg' in the Tidepool upload code. This was implemented in commit b244d174fa4fbf90835e09584078812359a8b587.

distilled.title: Bolus delivery % only for cob and Carbs !?
distilled.symptom: The option 'Deliver this part of bolus wizard result' applies to all components of the bolus wizard calculation, which can lead to overdosing when multiple consecutive carb entries are made within a short time period. For example, entering 60g of carbs in one entry results in 2.93U, but entering 45g then 15g results in 4.02U total, which is more than needed.
distilled.cause: The bolus wizard calculates a single dose for the end of DIA and applies the 'Deliver this part of bolus wizard result' percentage to all components (BG, trend, IOB, etc.), not just to carbs. This causes overdosing when multiple carb entries are made because each entry gets the full percentage applied, leading to cumulative insulin that exceeds the intended dose.
distilled.fix: The issue was resolved by a commit referenced by MilosKozak: https://github.com/nightscout/AndroidAPS/commit/6616be42791eb8ced53ee6ec2d1f878c1629c897. The commit likely changes the behavior so that the percentage applies only to carbs (COB and new carbs), as proposed by szantos.
distilled.evidence_quote: The option "Deliver this part of bolus wizard result" does what it says, but does it safely represent most user's intention? An overdosing may occur if there are multiple consecutive carb entries within a short time period.

The commit likely changes the behavior so that the percentage applies only to carbs (COB and new carbs), as proposed by szantos.   The option "Deliver this part of bolus wizard result" does what it says, but does it safely represent most user's intention? An overdosing may occur if there are multiple consecutive carb entries within a short time period.

distilled.title: Pumpe ICT - lokales Profil mit falschen Kombinationen
distilled.symptom: When MDI (ICT) is selected and the profile is edited, a basal rate is mandatory. On MDI, basal is provided by long-acting insulin whose action curve is not documented, so entering a basal rate in U/h is not meaningful. It is unclear how AndroidAPS calculates this, and if it is not considered in the bolus wizard, a basal rate of 0 should be allowed.
distilled.cause: The thread does not establish a root cause beyond the design requirement that a basal rate must be entered; MilosKozak explains that a basal rate of 0 is impossible due to internal calculations, but basal IOB is always zero because TBR cannot be changed on MDI.
distilled.fix: The suggested workaround is to enter a constant basal rate equal to the total daily long-acting insulin divided by 24 hours. For example, 20 U of Lantus or Toujeo per day gives a basal rate of 0.83 U/h. Additionally, the documentation should be updated to explain this.

distilled.title: Wear tiles, menus and settings aren't translated for Norwegian language
distilled.symptom: In the wear app for AAPS/AAPSClient, most icons in tiles, menu text, and settings are not translated to Norwegian, even though the main AAPS app is translated. Only 'Cancel' appears as 'Avbryt' in the temp-target tile; other tiles and settings remain in English. Changing AAPS language to English changes 'Avbryt' to 'Cancel', but other tiles stay English regardless of AAPS language.
distilled.cause: The Norwegian translation is associated with the language code 'no' (Norwegian), but Android's default system language for Norway is Norwegian Bokmål, which uses the code 'nb'. The app's resources are in 'values-no-rNO', but Android expects 'values-nb-rNO' for Norwegian Bokmål, so the translations are not applied.
distilled.fix: Create a new subfolder 'values-nb-rNO' in wear resources and copy the string file from 'values-no-rNO' into it. This fixed the tiles translation issue locally. Additionally, Norwegian Bokmål was added to Crowdin and the old Norwegian translations were uploaded, and the fix was confirmed in dev build fdc9ac1b.
distilled.evidence_quote: I asked @olorinmaia to create within wear resources a new subfolder `values-nb-rNO` and copy paste in it the string file included into `values-no-rNO` => It fixed the tiles translation issue for him...

distilled.title: Medtrum pump driver default setting and concerns
distilled.symptom: The Medtrum Nano pump driver does not default to the pump standard settings (terminate after three days and 8 hours grace period) and does not support low reservoir and empty alerts, which can cause issues overnight and when out for the day.
distilled.cause: The driver's default settings and lack of support for low reservoir and empty alerts were not aligned with pump standard behavior.
distilled.fix: The driver was updated to enable patch expiration by default and add an option to show non-critical pump alerts including low reservoir warning at 20 units. Also, the no connection alarm is forced to enabled with 30 minutes threshold for the Medtrum driver.

distilled.title: UAM SMBs with Libre 2

distilled.cause: The restriction is tied to an old Libre 1 issue where a MiaoMiao or similar Bluetooth interface could report flat BG values instead of an error during signal loss; this led to SMB features being gated for Libre-family sensors. distilled.fix: MilosKozak committed change 0771b6d which makes Libre 2 and Libre 3 work with SMB Always once the BG source provides proper identification.

distilled.title: Wrong COB in AAPS due to dependenies of I/C an ISF on carbimpact and therfore the calc of carbdecay in combination with Autosens
distilled.symptom: Wrong display of COB in AAPS, leading to incorrect bolus calculator suggestions and potentially too much or too little insulin, which can be dangerous, especially in parental setups. The issue is observed when Autosens adjusts ISF, altering the ratio of ISF to I/C and thus affecting carb decay calculation.
distilled.cause: COB calculation in AAPS is based on profile values of ISF and I/C. Autosens adjusts ISF only (in oref decision algorithm), which changes the carbimpact (ISF/IC ratio) and thus the carb decay calculation, leading to incorrect COB display.
distilled.fix: The thread does not provide a definitive fix. Suggestions include turning off Autosens for consistent COB decay, using autotune to determine real ratios, and adjusting min_5m_carbimpact. The user found that keeping carbimpact constant by adjusting ISF and I/C together helps, but this is not a formal fix.

distilled.fix: Turn OFF DynISF to test if COB values return to normal. Additionally, COB decaying is improved in version 3.3.0-dev-e.

distilled.title: PR3487 Unattended settings export.
distilled.symptom: The issue describes a feature request to enable unattended settings exports in AAPS, which currently require manual entry of the master password for encryption. The goal is to allow automatic exports without user interaction, such as scheduled exports via automation or after activating pumps.
distilled.fix: The thread describes a proposed implementation: adding an option in maintenance settings to enable/disable unattended exports. When enabled, the master password is securely stored encrypted on the phone's Android DataStore, with the encryption key protected by the Android KeyStore. The password expires after 4 weeks with a 1-week grace period. The feature is implemented via a new automation for scheduling exports. The PR was merged with dev.
distilled.evidence_quote: When the "unattended exports" option is enabled in maintenance preferences, the entered password is encrypted and securely stored on the user's phone (not in AAPS). Subsequent exports will no longer require the user to enter the master password until it expires or is reset.

distilled.title: Unable to Install or Upgrade AAPSClient on Android 14 (Samsung Galaxy S23 Ultra)
distilled.symptom: Unable to install or upgrade AAPSClient on Samsung Galaxy S23 Ultra (Android 14). Upgrading gives 'App not installed as package conflicts with an existing package.' Fresh install gives Google Play Protect warning and then same package conflict error.
distilled.cause: Android limitation: apps that use the same permission must be signed with the same key. A new permission in AAPSClient 3.3 to allow sending data to watch from multiple sources causes conflict with AAPS installed on same phone, which is signed with a different keystore.
distilled.fix: Compile AAPSClient yourself with the same keystore as AAPS, or do not have both AAPS and AAPSClient installed on the same phone.

distilled.title: [Bug 3.3.1.3] AAPSclient does not fetch data from NS
distilled.symptom: AAPSClient suddenly stops receiving data from NS several times a day. Hitting 'deliver now' fetches data at once. Occurs with or without websockets. Started on version 3.3.1.3.
distilled.cause: The issue is caused by glucose data not being uploaded to Nightscout using NSClientV3. If data is uploaded by another app (e.g., Juggluco) using v1 or not v3, AAPSClient using v3 will not receive it.
distilled.fix: Ensure that the glucose data is uploaded to Nightscout using NSClientV3. For Juggluco users, enable 'xdrip Broadcast' in Juggluco and set glucose source in AAPS to xDrip+, and configure AAPS to save glucose values to Nightscout. Alternatively, one user fixed it by deactivating nightscout cloud upload in xdrip+ application.
distilled.evidence_quote: If you don't receive data using v3 it only does mean it is not uploaded using v3. This is directly against best practice to let only AAPS upload to NS

distilled.title: Pod fault 049 when AAPS tries set a zero temp basal and a time change event has just occured
distilled.symptom: AAPS 2.8.2 suddenly reports pod fault 049 (INSULIN_DELIVERY_COMMAND_ERROR) and the pod is lost. The error occurs when AAPS sets a long zero temp basal, and during that period a time change event occurs; when the zero temp basal expires, AAPS tries to set a new temp basal but fails with pod fault 49.
distilled.cause: The code in OmnipodPumpPlugin.timezoneOrDSTChanged ignores time change events that are not DST or time zone changes, so the pod's time is not updated when the phone time changes (e.g., manual time adjustment). This leads to a pod fault when a zero temp basal expires after such a time change.
distilled.fix: Remove the code that prevents the pod time from being updated when a time change event is received and the time change is not a DST or time zone change, so the pod time is always updated when the phone time is updated. A patch (always_update_podtime.patch.zip) was applied and worked for 7 months with only one pod fault. Later, a PR (nightscout/AndroidAPS#726) was proposed to update time only if the last event was more than 24 hours ago.
distilled.evidence_quote: I removed the code that prevents the time in the pod from beeing updated when a time change event is received and the time change is not a DST change or a time zone change. This means that the time on the pod is now allways updated when the time on the phone is updated.

distilled.title: Profile Change to < 100% ends in error „Basalwert wurde durch den kleinstmöglichen Wert ersetzt: Profilwechsel“
distilled.symptom: In version 3.2, switching the profile to 80% works without trouble, but in the current version, profile changes to less than 100% result in an error message: 'Basalwert wurde durch den kleinstmöglichen Wert ersetzt: Profilwechsel'.
distilled.cause: The profile contains a basal rate of 0.05, which is the minimum allowed value. When the profile is reduced to a percentage below 100%, the basal rate would go below the minimum, causing the error.
distilled.fix: Change the basal rate in the profile from 0.05 to a higher value (e.g., 0.06 or 0.07) so that after percentage reduction it stays above the minimum. The user changed it to 0.06 and could then switch to 90%.

distilled.title: Preselection of hypo TT in carb UI
distilled.symptom: When entering carbs while low, the carb UI preselects 'start hypo TT', which can cancel an existing activity TT with a higher and longer duration. This can lead to the target resetting to default and the loop giving too much insulin, causing a severe hypo.
distilled.cause: The carb UI preselects 'start hypo TT' even when a higher and longer TT is already set, causing the hypo TT to override the activity TT.
distilled.fix: The issue was fixed by a patch (PR #4339) that changes the logic so that hypo TT is not automatically selected when there is already a high TT > 100 mg/dl or 5.5 mmol/L with a duration longer than the preset hypo TT duration.

distilled.title: AAPS Xdrip sends continuously and keeps app awake and burns battery
distilled.symptom: Phone becomes warm when not in use, battery usage shows AAPS taking 80% and draining 30% in a couple of hours. Xdrip logs in AAPS show it continuously sending hundreds of BG readings repeatedly, and once it approaches the end of the queue, it falls back several hundred readings and starts again. This goes on continuously until the app is force killed.
distilled.cause: The issue is triggered when a new BG entry arrives and is added to the queue while the Xdrip queue send is being processed, causing the queue resend to loop and never recover. This was observed when Juggluco sends a BG entry to AAPS in the middle of a sync.
distilled.fix: The issue was fixed by a commit referenced by MilosKozak: https://github.com/nightscout/AndroidAPS/commit/854833857f4b872db0966f3acc01422062eba574. Additionally, a workaround is to force kill the app, and configuration advice includes disabling sending of BG from AAPS when using xDrip as source, and ensuring only xDrip sends BG data to NS.

distilled.title: Medtronic 722 Version 2.2A Orange Pro fails to connect.
distilled.symptom: After updating to version 3.4.0.0 on a XIAOMI 14 phone, the Orange Pro Link app is unable to connect to the Medtronic 722 Version 2.2A insulin pump. After the first successful connection, the basal rate can be read, and the pump's time and settings can be retrieved. However, during subsequent connection attempts, the pump status shows a connection failure. It is impossible to connect to the pump to deliver bolus insulin or adjust the basal rate. Version 3.3.2.1 functions properly without these issues.
distilled.cause: The issue is caused by a migration bug in the Medtronic Encoding setting during version upgrade to 3.4.0.0. The display names for FourByteSixByteLocal and FourByteSixByteRileyLink were swapped in the code, leading to incorrect encoding behavior after upgrade.
distilled.fix: Go to the 'Medtronic Encoding' setting and switch the option from one to another (toggle it). This completely fixed the issue. A pull request #4526 was created to fix the underlying bug, and it is recommended to mention in release notes that if pump work is unstable after upgrade to or from 3.4.0.0, try switching the Medtronic Encoding setting.
