distilled.title: aaps-ci.yml does‘t allow line breaks in KEYSTORE_BASE64
distilled.symptom: The GitHub Actions workflow aaps-ci.yml does not allow line breaks in the KEYSTORE_BASE64 secret, which causes issues when the secret is generated using certutil on Windows, as it produces multi-line base64 output.
distilled.cause: The user generated the base64 secret using certutil on Windows, which produces multi-line base64 output, and the workflow's echo command does not handle line breaks in secrets.
distilled.fix: The suggested fix is to change the echo command to use a heredoc-style syntax to allow line breaks in the secret, but the maintainers argue that using the provided aaps-ci-preparation.html tool generates a single-line base64 and avoids the issue, so the change may not be needed.
distilled.evidence_quote: Please change the line echo "KEYSTORE_BASE64=${{ secrets.KEYSTORE_BASE64 }}" >> $GITHUB_ENV to echo "KEYSTORE_BASE64<<EOF" >> $GITHUB_ENV echo "${{ secrets.KEYSTORE_BASE64 }}" >> $GITHUB_ENV echo "EOF" >> $GITHUB_ENV or something else, so that line breaks in the secret KEYSTORE_BASE64 created during base64 encoding of the keystore.jks witch certutil would work.

distilled.title: Safety issue! Medtrum Nano pump (on-body) was reported falling back to priming stage after activation failed.
distilled.symptom: At least 2 users reported a situation where the Medtrum Nano, while already on body with needle pressed, fell back to priming stage, administering full priming insulin (up to 10 Units). One user experienced severe hypoglycemia with glucose dropping from 180 to 20 mg/dL.
distilled.cause: The root cause is a combination of two issues: (1) a BLE disconnect during ATTACH_PATCH causes the pump state to regress from PRIMED to FILLED, and (2) the retry activation flow in MedtrumRetryActivationConnectFragment.kt line 39 force moves to PRIME when it sees FILLED state, leading to re-priming while the patch is already on body.
distilled.fix: The fix is a commit referenced by MilosKozak: https://github.com/nightscout/AndroidAPS/commit/66baca4dc1772deb4661d1f8861d5b98fcf4934f. The thread does not specify the exact code changes.
distilled.evidence_quote: When BLE disconnected at 06:20:24 and reconnected at 06:20:28, the `SynchronizePacket` reported the pump state as `FILLED` instead of `EJECTED`/`PRIMED`. This caused the internal `SetupStep` to regress from `PRIMED` back to `FILLED`, making all subsequent activation attempts fail.

distilled.title: Issues when doing profile switch on DANA R
distilled.symptom: Performing a profile switch often leads to problems: multiple notifications that profile was updated, lots of communication with pump, and sometimes unable to properly connect and update basal in the pump. Logs show multiple threads trying to connect to pump simultaneously.
distilled.cause: Multiple instances of CommandQueue are created, each registering to handle profile switches, leading to concurrent handling. The independentConnect method creates new CommandQueue instances that are not properly disposed, causing multiple threads to attempt pump communication.
distilled.fix: The fix was to clear the disposable in the independentConnect method by adding `tempCommandQueue.disposable.clear()` at the end of independentConnect, as suggested by MilosKozak. This was later committed in commit fcf7faa3e05daf9c408821de1677ca1a6b6d7ab1, and the user confirmed it solved the issues.

distilled.title: Intermittent Omnipod Dash bolus failures — BusyException race in OmnipodDashBleManagerImpl, more pronounced on Atlas (InPlay BLE) pods
distilled.symptom: Intermittent bolus delivery failures ("Failed to send the command") with Omnipod Dash. Pod history shows repeated failures at the same timestamp followed by eventual success. The issue appears correlated with the newer Atlas (InPlay BLE) pod hardware generation versus the older SAW (TWI Board) generation.
distilled.cause: The root cause was identified via logcat capture as a U200 insulin concentration conversion issue: the loop calculated an SMB of 0.05 U, but the U200 conversion halved it to 0.025 before reaching the pod command builder, which requires a multiple of 0.05. This causes an IllegalArgumentException at ProgramBolusCommand$Builder.setNumberOfUnits, before any BLE communication. The BusyException race was initially suspected but ruled out after testing.
distilled.fix: Update to a version including commit 2e184102e1, which fixed the bolus size issue. The user confirmed the fix and closed the issue.
distilled.evidence_quote: Fixed in commit 2e184102e1. Closing, thank you!

distilled.title: ProfileFunctionImpl reads EPS.originalEnd directly for remaining-time display, producing garbage duration (e.g. "32399999998h")
distilled.symptom: The home-screen widget and Overview ribbon show an absurd remaining duration (e.g. "32399999998h") for a running temporary ProfileSwitch, instead of a plausible duration.
distilled.cause: The root cause is in ProfileSwitchExtension.kt: when parsing legacy NSClientV3 ProfileSwitch documents, it uses originalDuration instead of duration, corrupting the duration at the source. Additionally, ProfileFunctionImpl.getProfileName() reads EPS.originalEnd directly, which is documented as unused and unreliable, leading to garbage display when the stored originalEnd is stale or mismatched.
distilled.fix: The fix is to derive the end time from timestamp + originalDuration instead of trusting the stored originalEnd in ProfileFunctionImpl.getProfileName(), and to correct the parsing in ProfileSwitchExtension.kt to use duration instead of originalDuration when parsing legacy NSClientV3 ProfileSwitch documents.
distilled.evidence_quote: Thanks @MilosKozak for finding and fixing the actual root cause directly (`52056ebeb4` / `6bdbf1498`, `ProfileSwitchExtension.kt`: `originalDuration` vs `duration` when parsing legacy NSClientV3 `ProfileSwitch` documents).

distilled.title: 2.8.2 master / Arrow direction bug
distilled.symptom: In AAPS 2.8.2, the arrow direction on the main screen is often horizontal even when glucose is rising or falling, while the AAPS watchface and xDrip+ show a correct sloped arrow. This discrepancy is confusing and potentially dangerous.
distilled.cause: AAPS main screen uses the arrow direction provided by the BG source (e.g., xDrip+ or Dexcom app), which may be calculated differently (e.g., using a longer time interval or updated history values) than the arrow calculated by AAPS for the watchface, which uses a 5-minute delta. distilled.title: [3.0-beta1] New profile is not correctly shown after profile switch if the new profile has the same content as the old
distilled.symptom: After cloning a profile and editing only its name, then saving and activating it, the profile name in the top of the main display does not change. The new profile is saved correctly and the profile switch is logged, but the display of the profile name does not update. This occurs when the new profile has the same content as the old one; if content differs, there is no problem.
distilled.cause: In AAPS 3.0, the logic distinguishes between profile switch (PS) and effective profile switch (EPS). A new EPS is created only if the requested PS is different from the current EPS and the new profile is taken into account after confirmation from the pump. If only the name is changed and the content is the same, no new EPS is created, so the displayed profile name (taken from current EPS) does not update.
distilled.fix: The behavior was changed in beta3 so that a change in name is also a reason for updating the EPS. For users on earlier betas, a workaround is to perform a profile switch with a percentage (e.g., xx%) and then another one with 100% to force an EPS update.
distilled.evidence_quote: this is by design now. 3.0 distinguish between profile switch (PS) (something that user wants) and effective profile switch (EPS - setting loaded into pump and used for calculation). AAPS create new EPS if asked PS is different to current EPS and new profile takes into a count after confirmed from pump. Thus EPS will have different (later) timestramp. in case you only change name and do PS, no new EPS is created.

distilled.title: Crash on changing Overview graph granularity
distilled.symptom: When changing the granularity of the graph on the Overview tab, AAPS crashes. Tap-hold on the graph to change granularity two or three times causes a crash. Later, after a dev build, the crash is resolved but the UI becomes non-responsive and an 'AndroidAPS isn't responding' dialog appears.
distilled.cause: Changing the scale requires recalculating data in the past, which is CPU-intensive. On slow phones it takes tens of seconds, and pressing multiple times restarts recalculation, taking even more time.
distilled.fix: A PR (#911) was proposed that pre-calculates all scaling possibilities for the last 24 hours, eliminating the need for additional calculation during scaling changes. Testing confirmed it resolves the performance issues.
distilled.evidence_quote: I could improved it with doing during prepare data all scaling possibilities for the last 24hours (6h scaling, 12h scaling, 18hour scaling, 24 hour scaling, with and without prediction) It worked fine in overview because no additional calculation was required during any change of scaling done in overview

distilled.title: Project doesn't build
distilled.symptom: The project fails to build with Android Studio 3.5, with errors in wear dependencies and manifest merger failures. Users report various build errors and difficulty getting the project to compile.
distilled.cause: The build failures are due to regressions introduced by Android Studio and poor stewardship of the maven repositories by Google, as stated by jamorham. Specific issues include missing wearable dependencies and manifest merger conflicts.
distilled.fix: Workarounds include using Android Studio 3.4.1, uninstalling and cleaning Android Studio caches, and manually editing build files. wkochFPV provided specific steps: uncheck 'Only sync the active variant' in settings, add a meta-data element with tools:replace to the wear manifest, and change the google-services classpath to 3.2.0. Later, the project builds with current versions after merging PR #1160.

distilled.title: Database Import should not overwrite existing data
distilled.symptom: When importing an old database into xDrip+ on a new phone, the existing data is overwritten, causing loss of new values. Also, after import, the calibration for a running Dexcom G6 sensor is lost, forcing recalibration with blood.
distilled.cause: The current procedure is a complete restore of a backup database, which overwrites all existing data. The menu item is incorrectly named 'Import database' when it actually performs a restore.
distilled.fix: The menu item was renamed from 'Import' to 'Restore' to clarify behavior. There is no capability to import without overwriting; users should transfer the database before setting up the new phone as a collector. For Android 11 issues, refer to issue #1705.
distilled.evidence_quote: We have renamed the menu item from "Import" to "Restore" to avoid this confusion. There is currently no capability to import a database leaving the existing database intact.

distilled.title: uploader Battery Stuck on latest release
distilled.symptom: The battery status got stuck at 2% on the Sony Z3C used as an uploader after updating to version 1704030800. Deleting documents, restarting Azure, and rebooting the phone had no effect, and the issue disappeared after rolling back to version 1701201513.
distilled.cause: The xDripKit bridge/wixel device was reporting a bogus/stuck 2-3% battery value, and this bridge battery reading was uploaded to Nightscout and shown in the battery pill, so the correct Sony uploader battery percentage was not displayed.
distilled.fix: Update to the 25 April Nightly and uncheck 'Upload bridge battery' under Cloud Upload -> API Upload -> Extra Options to stop uploading the broken bridge battery to Nightscout. Optionally set DEVICESTATUS_ADVANCED=true in Nightscout environment variables to see the individual battery values on hover. The user confirmed unchecking the option resolved the issue.
distilled.evidence_quote: Okay, so the 25th April Nightly contains a new option within `Cloud Upload` -> `API Upload` -> `Extra Options` which is a checkbox for `Upload bridge battery` which you can uncheck if your bridge battery sensor is broken and this should stop it being uploaded to Nightscout.

distilled.title: Problems with LinearTrapezoidInsulin.java [Incorrect Boundary Conditions]
distilled.symptom: The LinearTrapezoidInsulin.java equations have incorrect boundary conditions because the value of 'onset' is not properly accounted for when applying boundary conditions during integration. This causes IOB values at transition points to not match, resulting in a kink in the IOB curve, and IOB does not become zero at the end of the insulin duration. The impact is more pronounced for insulins with larger onset and shorter life, such as Toujeo.
distilled.cause: The root cause is that the algorithm calculating IOB and iActivity was completely changed. The old algorithm needed a stepwise schema to calculate iActivity, while the new one uses a formula. The old algorithm has a one-step decay (5 minutes) before 'time', causing a timeshift. As a result, treatments.ioBForGraph_new starts exactly one timeslice before 'time' of the old one, and the new algorithm has to compensate. This timeshift leads to the observed issues, including IOB not being zero at the end.
distilled.fix: The thread does not state a definitive fix that was implemented. The user peeyes-dev provided updated equations and code, and stephencmorton confirmed they look correct, but there is no statement that they were merged or that a specific fix was applied. The issue was closed due to inactivity.

So the "old" one has a one step decay (5 minutes) before "time" and that's a (lets say) timeshift.

distilled.cause: A debug discovery of the Dexcom device shows the authentication characteristic (F8083535-849E-531C-C594-30F1F86A4EA5) advertises as WRITE and INDICATE, while xDrip attempts to do a READ operation in Ob1G5StateMachine, producing the repeated GATT read failures on Firefly transmitters.

distilled.title: xDrip+ refreshrate
distilled.symptom: xDrip+ with Nightscout refreshes BG data every 10 minutes, but the sensor sends data every 5 minutes, causing a delay.

distilled.fix: A new setting was added in the latest Nightly release (2023.11.21) that lets you delay when the follower reads from Nightscout, when Nightscout follower is selected as the data source.

distilled.title: libre 2 oop algorithm
distilled.symptom: When using the OOP algorithm with Libre 2, calibrated values are transferred to AndroidAPS, but uncalibrated values are transmitted to Nightscout, making evaluation or monitoring by Nightscout incorrect.
distilled.cause: The OOP algorithm cannot be calibrated, and the raw data from Libre 2 has a minimum value of 40, which prevents large intercept calibration. The thread also indicates that the issue is related to the calibration plugin not being applied to data sent to Nightscout.
distilled.fix: RainerTischnet describes a workaround: connect MM2 with xDrip, enable OOP algorithm, then in settings/advanced settings/advanced calibration choose 'xDrip original', calibrate, then export settings to XML, edit the XML to set 'calibrate_external_libre_algorithm' to true, import settings back, and set calibration plugin to none. This allows normal calibration to run with Nightscout and AAPS.

distilled.title: Code to communicate with Accucheck Guide
distilled.symptom: The user wants to code communication with an Accucheck Guide glucose meter but cannot find the BLE part that handles it, and is unsure whether it uses Bluetooth or USB.
distilled.cause: The Accucheck Guide does not have the GLUCOSE CONTEXT characteristic, which causes the program to get stuck in the queue if not removed.
distilled.fix: In the BluetoothGlucoseMeter class, modify the list of characteristics to remove the GLUCOSE CONTEXT characteristic (similar to what was done for Diamond Mobile Mini), and use the command Bluetooth_CMD.write(GLUCOSE_SERVICE, RECORDS_CHARACTERISTIC, RecordsCmdTx.getAllRecords(), "request all readings") to get data.

distilled.title: Starting a new sensor without queueing a "stop sensor" first
distilled.symptom: When starting a new sensor, if the xDrip UI is still in 'running' state and the user forgets to stop the sensor before placing the transmitter, the newly placed sensor receives a 'stopped' event and cannot be started anymore.
distilled.cause: The xDrip UI still shows 'running' state after an old sensor has been stopped, and if a new sensor is placed without stopping the UI first, the queued 'Stop Sensor' item is sent to the new transmitter, causing the new sensor to be stopped.
distilled.fix: A brute force method: wait for the transmitter's connection interval to reset to 0, then wait 10 seconds, stop sensor, and immediately clear the queue. Then restart the phone; for G6, xDrip will auto start its session.
distilled.evidence_quote: Wait for it to reset to 0. Then, wait 10 seconds. Now, stop sensor. As soon as you approve stopping sensor, clear the queue. If you do that exactly as I have explained, you will stop the xDrip session without stopping the session on the transmitter.

distilled.title: Unable to fully perform calibration on 8K series G6 transmitter with latest nightly (67014b0-20202.07.25)
distilled.symptom: All attempts to calibrate result in 'Got invalid impossible slope calibration!'. The calibration is accepted by the transmitter but xdrip doesn't register as such and stays in 'initial calibration' stage. Was working on previous transmitter (81 series).
distilled.cause: The issue is caused by the Firefly firmware (8G and later transmitters) in combination with xDrip, which has limitations on calibration when the difference between current BG and calibration value is too large (more than 15-20%). Additionally, xDrip issues confusing messages when calibrating an 8KXXXX transmitter, and the calibration command is called initial calibration even for subsequent calibrations.
distilled.fix: Workaround: calibrate in MAX 20% steps and wait at least 12 hours between calibrations. Also, use the syringe icon for entering calibrations and follow settings as per issue #1310. The thread does not provide a definitive fix; it suggests that the confusing messages need to be addressed by developers.
distilled.evidence_quote: You cannot calibrate with too big differences of current BG vs the calibration value. As a rule of thumb don't enter calibrations with more than 15-20% difference. Workaround if your real BG is *really* that far off => calibrate in MAX 20% steps and always wait a few hours until the next calibration.

distilled.title: xdrip+ not synchronising all glucose data points from Nightscout when the measurement insert rate is > 1/5 minutes (libre)
distilled.symptom: When using xDrip+ as a Nightscout follower with a Libre sensor and glimp as uploader, the BG graph has missing data points. The follower does not query enough data from Nightscout, resulting in gaps in the graph, especially when data is inserted more frequently than every 5 minutes.
distilled.cause: The MissedReadingsEstimator assumes one reading every five minutes (DEXCOM_PERIOD), so the follower requests too few entries when the uploader inserts data more frequently (e.g., every minute).
distilled.fix: The issue was addressed by changing the NUM_VALUES constant in BgGraphBuilder.java to not divide by 5 (i.e., (60) * 24 instead of (60/5)*24) and by adding de-duplication to the expected 5-minute window when the brief_mode parameter is set. The fix was included in the 2022.07.21 release and the Aug 1st nightly.
distilled.evidence_quote: The issue is mostly because of the bug in the nightscout follower code which allows records to be stored at a higher frequency than the collector would typically allow. I think the best way to address this is a de-duplicator in BgReading which I will work on.

distilled.title: Dexcom sensor state inconsistently shown
distilled.symptom: The Dexcom sensor state is not consistently shown across the main screen, menu and system status. After a sensor session ends the main screen says 'Stopped' while the menu still shows 'Stop sensor'; after starting a new sensor, xDrip can still show 'stopped' and warm-up messages even though the sensor has started. This is confusing, especially at sensor session beginnings/ends.
distilled.cause: The thread identifies the original inconsistency as partly a hang-over from when xDrip supported coexisting native and non-native data: within xDrip, a sensor session isn't strictly tied to the native Dexcom session.
distilled.fix: A nightly update added transitional states (for example, showing 'Starting Sensor' instead of 'Stopped' when a sensor is about to be started), which Navid states addressed the original menu/main-screen inconsistency. For sensor replacement cases, the thread describes a workaround: after stopping, wait for the transmitter to perform a final read, remove it, and keep it disconnected for at least 10 minutes before inserting it in a new sensor.
distilled.evidence_quote: The latest nightly includes some transitional states which I think should resolve most of the problems described in this issue. For example when a sensor is about to be started it will say `Starting Sensor` instead of its current actual state, eg `Stopped`

distilled.title: Importing data didn't display data and wiped settings
distilled.symptom: After wiping xDrip app data and cache, restoring settings and importing the exported database reports success, but no data is imported and the restored settings are wiped again. Repeating the import gives the same blank screen and cleared settings. Other users report the same on Android 11/12: the import says success but no data appears.
distilled.fix: Switch to the new Google Drive cloud backup methodology instead of the legacy zip import/export. On the old phone, create a Cloud Backup via the three-dots menu > Import/Export features > Cloud Backup. On the new phone, download that backup file, then in Cloud Backup > SELECT BACKUP LOCATION choose USE ALTERNATE FILE to select the downloaded file and tap RESTORE FROM BACKUP. One user also succeeded by restoring the zip on an older Android 8 phone, uploading it to Google Drive, and restoring from there on the Android 11 phone.
distilled.evidence_quote: The solution is to switch to the new backup methodology to Google Drive. That means when you buy a new phone, backup the database from the old phone using the new backup methodology, Google Drive Backup. Then, restore it on the new phone using the Google Drive Backup methodology. If you do that and it doesn't work, please let us know.

distilled.title: G6 Timestamp Issue when newly activated.
distilled.symptom: When first activating a G6 transmitter, xDrip incorrectly reports timestamps as negative for the first few hours because the transmitter's internal time starts from 0ms. This prevents xDrip from generating packets that need a timestamp (like backfill requests) for the first few hours after activation.
distilled.cause: The transmitter timestamp before transmitter start is being requested, likely from backfilling. The backfill window is not capped to the transmitter start time, so requests are made for times before the transmitter's internal clock reaches zero.
distilled.fix: Cap the backfill window to the transmitter start (or session start) time. The fix was implemented in the Nightly build of March 10, 2024, and tested successfully with G6 and G7.
distilled.evidence_quote: I expect this will come from backfilling and simply capping the backfill window to the transmitter start (or session start) would resolve the issue.

distilled.title: Dynamically Detect Dexcom Warm-Up Duration
distilled.symptom: xDrip assumes a 120 minute warmup when it starts a sensor, but some G6 transmitters have non-standard warmup durations. When a session is started from xDrip, the interface continues to count down 120 minutes and does not display the BG reading, which is confusing for users.
distilled.cause: xDrip assumes a fixed 120-minute warmup duration based on firmware version, rather than dynamically reading the actual warmup duration from the transmitter via the 0x52 opcode.
distilled.fix: Implement dynamic detection of warmup duration by issuing the 0x5202 command to the transmitter's Command UUID after authentication, which returns the actual warmup time (e.g., 120 minutes for stock G6, 60 minutes for stock G6+).
distilled.evidence_quote: xDrip assumes a 120 minute warmup when it starts a sensor. We do get dot points on the graph and broadcast data... But the xDrip interface continues to count down 120 minutes and doesn't display the BG reading.

distilled.title: Smart alert doesn't work
distilled.symptom: Despite having smart snoozing and smart alerting enabled, alerts are triggered when glucose is near an alert threshold but trending in the right direction (downward). The user reports getting woken by unnecessary alerts during the night.
distilled.cause: The smart alerting logic uses a paranoid approach: it only suppresses alerts if the glucose difference over the last 5 minutes is at least 4 mg/dL and over the last 10 minutes is at least 10 mg/dL in the correct direction. In the reported case, transient upward readings caused xDrip to see an upward trend, so the alert triggered even though the overall trend was downward.
distilled.fix: No definitive fix was provided in the thread. A change was made to high alerts only, and the issue was closed with the intention to later improve smart snooze and alert for low alerts as well.
distilled.evidence_quote: Smart snoozing and smart alerts means that the alert will not trigger in the case that there is a "real" movement in the correct direction. They have been implemented with a paranoid approach. So, for the alert not to trigger, the difference in the last 5 minutes should be at least 4 (mgdl), and the difference for the last 10 minutes should be at least 10 (mgdl).

distilled.symptom: The persistent notification for the foreground collector and the number icon use the same notification channel, so hiding one hides the other. The user wants to hide the persistent collector notification while keeping the number icon.
distilled.cause: The persistent foreground collector notification and the number icon share the same notification channel (Ongoing notification), so Android cannot hide one without the other.
distilled.fix: A separate notification channel was created for the number icon, but this results in two notifications. Instead, the developer made the existing notification very small as an alternative.
distilled.evidence_quote: I created a separate notification channel for the number icon. The problem is that we will end up with two different notifications! After you disable the persistent notification, you will have one notification. There is no way to eliminate the notification. Showing the number icon is done through a notification. So, I decided to follow your other preferences of having the option of making the existing notification very small.

distilled.cause: The slope/intercept calculation code does not check the generated values against the current calibration plugin's sanity limits, so it can produce intercept values above the hardcoded limit (e.g., 44), which are then rejected as invalid.

distilled.title: Dexcom Share: Ability to Specify Seconds Until Polling Retry or Allow Double Poll Retry
distilled.symptom: When following a Dexcom G6 via Dexcom Share, the xDrip follower polls every 5 minutes; if the reading hasn't reached the Dexcom Share servers yet (often in low cellular signal areas), it waits a hard-coded 20 seconds, retries once, and if that still fails it waits another 5 minutes. This causes readings to be 5–10 minutes behind 30–40% of the time.
distilled.cause: xDrip polls the Dexcom Share server at the expected reading time, but the reading is frequently not yet uploaded (especially with low cellular signal), and the single hard-coded 20-second retry is too short; when that fails xDrip gives up until the next 5-minute cycle. A contributor also suspected a bug in the shared anticipation code (`Anticipate.java`).
distilled.fix: Workaround used by some participants: set the follower phone's system time 10–15 seconds behind real time. A maintainer implemented an optional delay for the Dexcom Share follower in PR #3663, but it was never merged and the issue/PR were closed.
settings_changed: System time → 10-15 seconds behind real time
distilled.evidence_quote: What has alleviated having to manually restart the collector 50+ times each day was to use @olorinmaia suggestion to set the parent follower phone's system time 10-15 seconds behind real time.

distilled.title: G6 On new sensor start, data with timestamp before new sensor was started is sent to NS and AAPS
distilled.symptom: When a new G6 sensor is started, xDrip sends old data (data accumulated before the new sensor was started) to Nightscout and over the local broadcast. AAPS receives these duplicate Bg values and stops the loop.
distilled.cause: After starting a new G6 sensor, xDrip requests a backfill on the first reading; because de-duplication is filtered by sensor session, backfilled readings from the old sensor with slightly different timestamps are accepted and then broadcast/uploaded to NS/AAPS.
distilled.fix: Cap the backfill window start to the current sensor session start (commit 6f7c3660d6e140d914f24a155a0bcffa810ab4d8) so no data from before the current sensor session is backfilled; released in the January 14, 2022 nightly. The same change still needs to be applied to the wear collector before the issue can be fully closed.

The same change still needs to be applied to the wear collector before the issue can be fully closed. distilled.title: Ways to improve the Reminders feature

distilled.symptom: The y-axis (BG value) is auto-scaled to the highest level within the last 24h, which can make steep slopes appear flatter than they are and give confusing impressions. A single bad point can make the graph useless for 24 hours.
distilled.cause: The y-axis scaling is based on the highest value in the last 24 hours, which can be skewed by a single high reading (even a bad one) and remains scaled for 24 hours.

distilled.title: moved from heroku to google fine but looking to find the data api
distilled.symptom: After migrating from Heroku to Google Cloud, the user's Fitbit clock face (from pedantic avenger) requests a DATA API URL and fails with the new host. Another user reports that xDrip as follower gets 'NS entries download was not succesful:401 unautorized' when using the NS follower box.
distilled.cause: The thread explains that Heroku did not impose a limit on outgoing bandwidth, but on Google Cloud, if outgoing bandwidth goes over 1GB/month, it will not be free. To minimize egress by default, the AUTH_DEFAULT_ROLES variable is set to 'denied', which blocks unauthenticated read access, causing devices like Fitbit and xDrip that do not use tokens to fail.
distilled.fix: Change the Nightscout variable AUTH_DEFAULT_ROLES from 'denied' to 'readable' and restart the server. This is a workaround for devices that cannot use tokens. The thread also suggests using apps/devices that support tokens as the proper solution.
distilled.evidence_quote: The variable name is the following. AUTH_DEFAULT_ROLES The value it is set to now on your system must be: denied If you want to try the experiment, change it to: readable

distilled.title: Tidepool Authentication API Deprecation
distilled.symptom: Tidepool has deprecated its legacy authentication API after replacing it with Keycloak, and the old endpoints are being retired. xDrip's current integration uses these deprecated endpoints and starts a new auth session every time a fresh token is needed instead of refreshing the session token directly.
distilled.cause: Tidepool replaced its legacy authentication system with Keycloak in December 2022, deprecating the old API endpoints. xDrip was using the old flow and creating a new auth session for each token instead of using refresh tokens.
distilled.fix: xDrip implemented the new OpenID Connect authorization code flow with refresh tokens against Tidepool's Keycloak server. After a Keycloak bug causing 'invalid_grant' logouts was fixed and deployed, the new authentication mechanism was switched on as the default in xDrip and released on September 23.

distilled.title: Snooze locked phone
distilled.symptom: Snoozing an xDrip 'Low Alert' using the volume button of the phone no longer works. The user has to unlock the screen and swipe to snooze the sound. When the alert rings when the screen is already unlocked, volume buttons do not snooze; they only work after locking and unlocking the screen.
distilled.cause: The thread explains that snoozing an alert via volume buttons when the phone is locked has never been possible (see issue #73). The behavior is due to Android limitations: you cannot receive those broadcasts unless the screen is on or there is active audio playing.
distilled.fix: To snooze an alert while the phone is locked, change Android notification settings to show notification details on lock screen, and enable the xDrip setting that turns the screen on when there is a notification. Then, when an alert triggers, swipe the notification right to snooze.
settings_changed: Android notification settings → show notification details on lock screen
xDrip setting that turns the screen on when there is a notification → enabled
distilled.evidence_quote: By default, you cannot snooze an alert when your phone is locked.  But, you can change a few settings to make it possible. First, you need to change an Android notifications setting so that it would show notification details on lock screen. Then, there is a relatively new xDrip setting that turns the screen on when there is a notidication. After that, as soon as an alert triggers, you will see the notification on the screen of your phone, and swiping it right will snooze the alert with your phone still locked.

The behavior is due to Android limitations: you cannot receive those broadcasts unless the screen is on or there is active audio playing. To snooze an alert while the phone is locked, change Android notification settings to show notification details on lock screen, and enable the xDrip setting that turns the screen on when there is a notification. Then, when an alert triggers, swipe the notification right to snooze. Samsung Galaxy S10e Android 12 Android 8  By default, you cannot snooze an alert when your phone is locked.  But, you can change a few settings to make it possible. First, you need to change an Android notifications setting so that it would show notification details on lock screen. Then, there is a relatively new xDrip setting that turns the screen on when there is a notidication. After that, as soon as an alert triggers, you will see the notification on the screen of your phone, and swiping it right will snooze the alert with your phone still locked.

distilled.title: How to track/monitor more than one persons with one one smartphone (xDrip+ app)?
distilled.symptom: The user wants to follow more than one person (two Dexcom G4) with one phone, for example one xDrip Parakeet for person 1 and another xDrip Bluetooth or Parakeet feed for person 2. They ask if multiple instances of xDrip can be installed or if there is another way to monitor two people while carrying only one smartphone.
distilled.cause: A phone can run two xDrip instances, but the second one must be a specially built 'variant' because a normal second install of the same app is not possible under the same Android application identity/signing key. If someone else builds that variant, you will not have the original signing key and therefore cannot later build/install that exact same variant yourself.
distilled.fix: Run two xDrip instances on one phone: keep one as a normal xDrip Bluetooth installation and install the second one as an xDrip variant that can be an xDrip follower or read from a parakeet. To create the variant yourself, change the applicationId/package name (including in /wear/build.gradle for release builds); otherwise use the variant nightly builds supplied by jamorham from the shared Google Drive folder. Official and variant builds can coexist on the same phone.
distilled.evidence_quote:
One phone can run two instances of xDrip.
One can be a normal xDrip installation using BT.
The second one can read data from another xDrip (that is be an xDrip follower) or read data from a parakeet.
In order to install the second application you need to make a small change when building xDrip.

distilled.title: Blukon collector restart race condition
distilled.symptom: In some circumstances, xDrip restarts the collector even though it is communicating with Blukon, which can happen when 'Agressiv service restarts' is enabled or if the user forces a restart manually. This can lead to long reconnection times because xDrip waits 5 minutes each time.
distilled.cause: The collector restart logic does not check whether the Blukon device is actually communicating; it restarts based on missed reading service restarts, causing a race condition.
distilled.fix: Implement a static method `isCollecting()` in the Blukon class that returns true if data is being received, and use that to decide whether to restart the service instead of relying on `BgReading.last_within_millis()`. The method should be wired up to prevent restarts when communication is active.
distilled.evidence_quote: I think storing a timestamp of the last time blukon class received any data from the remote device and then we can use that (or a boolean method like `isCommunicating()` based on that timestamp to decide whether to restart the service instead of `BgReading.last_within_millis()` would make it more reliable.

distilled.title: BT Glucose Meters and Initial Calibration problems
distilled.symptom: When performing a finger prick with a Bluetooth glucose meter (e.g., Contour Next One) while xDrip is set to Auto Calibration and the initial calibration screen is open, the incoming BT reading overwrites the initial calibration prompt with a normal calibration prompt, causing the initial calibration screen to close or hide. Selecting yes records the value as a normal blood glucose reading, not as an initial calibration, and it never becomes a calibration because there is no data around it.
distilled.cause: The thread does not explicitly identify a root cause, but it is implied that xDrip's handling of BT readings does not distinguish between initial calibration and normal calibration, so incoming readings are treated as normal readings even when an initial calibration is pending.
distilled.fix: The suggested workaround from the maintainer is to tap on the square marker of the reading and choose to use it as a calibration, confirming that you want to use the point as a calibration. This allows manual calibration instead of relying on automatic calibration before initial calibrations are entered.
distilled.evidence_quote: In that case, you can tap on the square marker and tap on calibrate and confirm that you want to use the point as a calibration.

distilled.title: Remove duplicate Norwegian language in Crowdin and xDrip+
distilled.symptom: There are duplicate Norwegian language entries in Crowdin and xDrip+ ('Norwegian' and 'Norwegian Bokmal'), causing confusion for Norwegian users. The 'Norwegian' option is only 45% translated and is essentially an unfinished version of Norwegian Bokmål, while 'Norwegian Bokmal' is 100% translated and is the default system language for Norwegian phones.
distilled.cause: The 'no' language was added to Crowdin and xDrip+ by mistake, possibly due to a misunderstanding that there were two distinct Norwegian languages. In reality, Norwegian Bokmål (nb) is the standard written language, and 'no' is not a valid ISO code for Norwegian; it is just an incomplete duplicate of nb.
distilled.fix: Remove the 'no' language from Crowdin and xDrip+, change the forced language option value from 'no' to 'nb', create a legacy settings update feature to migrate users who had selected 'Norsk' (no) to 'nb', and remove the 'no' translated strings from the source tree. Also rename the display name for 'nb' to 'Norsk bokmål'.

Display name for nb → Norsk bokmål

distilled.title: Invalid G7 start time sent to AAPS
distilled.symptom: The Classic Status Page shows the start date of the previous sensor while the G5/G6/G7 status page and home screen show the correct sensor age; AAPS shows the same (incorrect) age as the Classic Status Page.
distilled.cause: xDrip maintains its own internal 'Sensor Start' time for the Classic Status Page and for what it sends to AAPS instead of using the G7 transmitter's reported start. If the old sensor session is not stopped in xDrip when switching to a new G7, that internal timer is not reset and an invalid old start time keeps being broadcast.
distilled.fix: Use Navid200's PR #3263, which makes xDrip stop basing the displayed/broadcast sensor start on the xDrip session start and instead read the G7 transmitter's start time to update the Classic Status Page and AAPS broadcast. Testers confirmed it corrects the Classic Status Page and AAPS sensor-age/treatment output.
distilled.evidence_quote: That PR stops caring about when you start the xDrip session. It looks at the transmitter and updates the classic status page and what is sends to AAPS from it.

distilled.title: xDrip can show an overlap when switching hardware data source
distilled.symptom: When switching the hardware data source from a G6 collector to Nightscout follower, xDrip shows overlapping readings (backfilled data overlaps with existing data). The overlap occurs when switching from G6 collector to Nightscout follower, but not when switching from Nightscout follower to G6 collector.
distilled.cause: The overlap is caused by xDrip backfilling data for a time period that already has readings, even if the timestamps are not exactly the same. The backfill does not check for existing data in the same time period.
distilled.fix: Starting with the xDrip Nightly release of July 17, 2024, xDrip will only backfill (G6 or G7) starting from the last existing reading. This avoids the possibility of an overlap. As of the 2025.03.23 release, this is fixed for G7 to G7 switch as well.

distilled.title: New upgrade broke high values
distilled.symptom: After updating, values above 300 show up as a low 30. For example, 319 on Freestyle Libre shows as 31. Everything above 270 shows up as 27 (low).
distilled.cause: The issue is caused by a numerical overflow due to values beyond the 12-bit coding. The 13th bit was removed from the calculation, causing high values to wrap around and appear as low values.
distilled.fix: Enable the 13th bit mask in xDrip settings: Settings -> Less Common Settings -> Calibration Settings -> use 13 bit ads mask. Alternatively, use another algorithm as described in LibreOOPAlgorithm. The 13bit mask mode is enabled by default in the latest nightly.

distilled.title: Consistent REST-API problem
distilled.symptom: Users are receiving consistent error messages (pop-up) on their Android smartphone when uploading to Nightscout via REST API. Some BG readings go through sporadically and laggy, and treatments do not show up in Nightscout.
distilled.cause: The issue was caused by an Azure App Service deployment that affected Android apps with older HTTP clients, leading to connection failures. The specific cause was the site config setting "http20Enabled" being set to true, which caused problems with HTTP/2.
distilled.fix: The workaround is to change the Azure site config setting "http20Enabled" to false via resources.azure.com, and optionally replace https with http in the REST API cloud upload URL in xDrip+, then restart the Azure site.
distilled.evidence_quote: Customers experiencing this issue can self-mitigate by updating the site config setting "http20Enabled" to false via resources.azure.com.

distilled.symptom: After updating the circuit to xBridge2 firmware with battery charge indicator resistors, the battery percentage readings are erratic: overnight it wouldn't charge above 40%, then depleted quickly to 20%, then jumped to 79% when plugged into a 1A charger, charged to 100% quickly, but dropped to 84% immediately after disconnecting.
distilled.cause: The xBridge2 battery indication is not a truly accurate measurement of battery capacity; it is only an indication based on battery voltage, not current in/out. The circuit design and off-the-shelf components cannot provide accurate readings.
distilled.fix: Use the Adafruit charger's red/green LED to know when charging is complete; do not remove the bridge from charging until the green LED is lit. The indication will then stay at 100% for a fair period. Under the current design, only a rough indication is possible.
distilled.evidence_quote: the xBridge2 battery indication is NOT a truly accurate measurement of battery capacity, it is only an indication.based on battery voltage, not a measurement based on current in/out like most mobile phones.

distilled.title: Race condition for "Disable Forced Wear on Missed Readings"
distilled.symptom: If you are force collecting via Wear, and switch off your phone, when you turn it on again, if the time delta is greater than the 'Disable Forced Wear on Missed Readings' value, the phone will disable forced Wear before Wear can sync and backfill BG data collected while the phone was off.
distilled.cause: The phone disables forced Wear before Wear can sync and backfill BG data collected while the phone was off, due to the time delta exceeding the 'Disable Forced Wear on Missed Readings' threshold.
distilled.fix: The issue was reported to no longer happen in recent releases, but the user notes that often the phone struggles to pick up missed readings stored in the Wear DB for several cycles (or at all) without rebooting the phone and watch, and during that time it can pass the threshold for 'Disable Forced' and the phone tries to take over. No specific fix was provided.

distilled.symptom: The user reports periods of total loss of connection with the G5 transmitter, requiring phone restart and forgetting the device to reconnect. distilled.fix: Uninstall the current Garmin Connect app and install an older version (Garmin Connect Mobile 4.1.5) from APKMirror, or perform a factory reset and uninstall Connect. Alternatively, use a 2017 version of Garmin Connect with a May 10th xDrip nightly version.

distilled.cause: The thread identifies a possible issue with Android 8.0 (Oreo) on Samsung devices causing Bluetooth problems, possibly related to a June 5 security patch. A user also found that the 'Allow blucon unbonding' option, which defaults to enabled, may cause pairing failures due to a bug in the code.
distilled.fix: Several workarounds are suggested: clearing the Bluetooth cache on the phone, disabling the 'Allow blucon unbonding' option (which resolved issues for one user), and using Glimp to maintain the Bluetooth connection. A Samsung security patch (G950FXXU2CRF1) was reported to fix issues on S8.
distilled.evidence_quote: I had horrible problems with it lately (on and off for months, after working great for a while), and then found a new option had been added: "Allow blucon unbonding", which defaults to enabled.  Turning this off seems to fix everything.

distilled.cause: xDrip only calculates its simulation IoB when the main graph is displayed as it is quite CPU intensive. The local web service's pebble endpoint had iob hardcoded to 0.
distilled.fix: A pull request (https://github.com/NightscoutFoundation/xDrip/pull/2897) was submitted and merged that implements IoB reporting in the /pebble endpoint.

distilled.title: Regression: false "Appears to have lost bonding, skipping this connect!" with Special Pairing Workaround since 2026.07.08 — lost readings
distilled.symptom: Since updating to a nightly containing commit 7213241f4, users with Special Pairing Workaround enabled get bursts of 'Appears to have lost bonding, skipping this connect!' messages. The bonding is not actually lost, but connects are skipped and readings are lost until the safety valve at 10 skips forces a connect, or the user re-pairs or restarts the app.
distilled.cause: Commit 7213241f4 added to onStartCommand in Ob1G5CollectionService.java: transmitterMAC = null; // clear on every service start. This causes isDeviceLocallyBonded() to return false because transmitterMAC is null, and in CONNECT_NOW state with Special Pairing Workaround on, the guard fires and skips connects.
distilled.fix: Do not treat 'MAC not known yet' as 'bonding lost'. Options: Call tryLoadingSavedMAC() at the top of the CONNECT_NOW case (or inside isDeviceLocallyBonded()) so the cached MAC is restored before the check, or require transmitterMAC != null in the skip condition. A proposed fix is in commit 712eac9b. Workaround: disable Special pairing workaround, forget BT device and re-pair, or rollback to release 2026.06.17.

distilled.symptom: xDrip loses connection to the miaomiao due to interference with 2.4 GHz WLAN, requiring manual Bluetooth scan and selection of the miaomiao to reconnect. This happens at varying frequencies depending on the environment.

distilled.title: Newest Android update 8.0
distilled.symptom: After updating a Samsung S7 Edge to Android 8.0 (Oreo) with Samsung Experience 9.0, replacing a Libre sensor with a BluCon transmitter fails to connect: the phone receives no initial data, never reaches calibration, and the transmitter never shows connected in xDrip, despite Bluetooth pairing working. The issue persists after clearing app cache/data and reinstalling, and the same setup works on a Samsung Note 4 with Android 6.0.1.
distilled.cause: The thread identifies the cause as a combination of Android 8.0 (Oreo) Bluetooth stack issues and the BLE module used in the BluCon (HM-10 or similar), which is incompatible with Oreo. Some users also note that the issue may be related to the xDrip version, as reverting to an older version helped.
distilled.fix: The thread suggests several workarounds: clearing Bluetooth app cache/data and reinstalling xDrip (temporary), reverting to an older xDrip version (e.g., 2018.01.22) which works with random disconnects, or using the latest nightly with OB1 collector (though not fully successful for all). The issue was marked as resolved by a maintainer after changes for Android 8.0 pairing, but no single definitive fix is stated.

distilled.fix: Ignore the checksum error; it is not a bug and retries happen automatically. Also, ensure the miaomiao is attached well to the sensor.

distilled.title: huawei EMUI Bluetooth issues and missed readings
distilled.symptom: Users with Huawei phones running EMUI experience missed readings due to BLE scanning issues when the screen is off. The log shows 'App is scanning too frequently on screen off'. Readings resume when the screen is woken.
distilled.cause: Huawei EMUI software performs its own BLE management, causing issues with scanning and connecting when the screen is off, leading to missed readings.
distilled.fix: For Huawei EMUI, set the app to manage manually in battery settings, enable auto-launch, secondary launch, and run in background, disable battery optimization for xDrip, lock the app in the app switcher, and on some devices set battery mode to Performance instead of Power Saving. On older EMUI versions without these options, the issue may persist and require a different phone.
distilled.evidence_quote: In Settings>Battery it needs to be put in Performance mode. I had it in Power Saveing mode.

distilled.cause: xDrip+ has built-in logic that checks if airplane mode is enabled and may not operate properly when airplane mode is on, even if Bluetooth is manually enabled.
distilled.fix: Use an ADB command to change the airplane_mode_radios setting so that airplane mode does not affect Bluetooth. Additionally, ensure that after a reboot, you are not in airplane mode initially; enter airplane mode after being on cell, with Bluetooth still enabled.

distilled.title: Nightscout follower - 5 min. delay
distilled.symptom: While following Nightscout page, data is between 5 and 10 minutes old. xDrip+ appears to pull data with a delay or not frequently enough, and it never catches up to the current time, always being about 5 minutes behind.
distilled.cause: The issue is with the Dexcom servers, as stated by a commenter. Additionally, the Nightscout Follow logic in xDrip+ may not be polling frequently enough.
distilled.fix: Decrease the Dexcom Share polling interval by setting BRIDGE_INTERVAL to 15000 (15 seconds) in Nightwatch settings, which almost completely eliminated the lag. Alternatively, changing the grace value in NightscoutFollowService.java to something bigger than 10 seconds (e.g., Constants.SECOND_IN_MS * 30) might fix the problem, but this was not tested.

distilled.title: xdrip api-secret correct url syntax
distilled.symptom: When using xDrip's local web service with an API secret set, requests like http://127.0.0.1:17580/status.json return 'Authentication failed - check api-secret', 'secret is required', and 'no secret supplied'. The service works without the secret.
distilled.cause: The API secret must be sent as a header, not as part of the URL (e.g., user:password@host syntax). The thread indicates that an API secret is not an authorization protocol that can be handled directly in the browser URL.
distilled.fix: Use a layer in between (e.g., an AJAX request with a JavaScript framework like jQuery) to set the 'api-secret' header. The secret should be the SHA1 hash in lowercase, as shown in the curl example: curl.exe -X DELETE -H "api-secret: 911eea185f5c758ac275687da8b7eab50ad720e5" -g https://...
distilled.evidence_quote: So, the api secret should be part of the header. I'm not sure how you are sending the requests, but something has to put the api-secret in the header.

distilled.title: G6 sensor restart problems with xDrip
distilled.symptom: After restarting a Dexcom G6 sensor after 10 days, the user initially saw a warm-up period but then got a 'sensor failed start' message. A notification 'Auto Start Sensor Requesting Restart' appears but clicking it does nothing. Restarting the collector and re-pairing the transmitter did not help.
distilled.cause: The thread does not explicitly identify a root cause, but opasha suggests that the sensor's gold dot area and the transmitter's black rubber tips may be dirty, causing connection issues. Also, the 0000 method is said to do nothing.
distilled.fix: The proven method described by opasha: Stop sensor, remove transmitter for at least 15 minutes, clean the sensor's gold dots and the transmitter's black rubber tips, reconnect, start sensor as new with the same code (not 0000), wait 2 hours and a few minutes for warm-up. This method was confirmed to work by mrazek.
distilled.evidence_quote: This is the proven way to make it work: 1) Stop Sensor 2) Remove the transmitter with thin plastic (guitar pick or glucometer test strip) - set a time for 15 minutes - no less 3) Wipe down the sensor's two gold dot area - this gets sweat/oil/soap/water on it, so it needs to be completely cleaned to be functional - anything in the way will cause errors - MAKE SURE TO KEEP THE TRANSMITTER NEAR YOUR PHONE DURING THIS TIME. 4) Carefully clean the black rubber tips on your sensor on your arm - this is the point of contact those gold circle sensors make from your transmitter. Yes, they both need to be clean before contact with each other - I have tested this many times - the cleaner the contact, the longer your sensor can last - I have done 2 re-start sessions and got up to 27 days once. 5) After the 15 minutes are up and sensor and transmitter are cleaned, reconnect them and make sure your phone is still connected to your transmitter 6) Start Sensor as if brand new - enter the present time and date when asked and enter the same code for your transmitter - do not do the 0000 method - it does nothing 7) Wait 2 hours and a few minutes (for the final warm up) and it will automatically resume

distilled.title: Unable to read Miaomiao data after upgrade to Android 10
distilled.symptom: After upgrading to Android 10, xDrip can see the MiaoMiao device over Bluetooth but fails to connect or receive data. One user reports that switching to Wear collection produces only one reading before failing; another with Android 9 also reports the same problem. Some users later report nightly missed readings due to Bluetooth disconnects.
distilled.cause: The principal reported cause is an Android 10 Bluetooth communication issue with MiaoMiao: xDrip recognizes the MiaoMiao on Bluetooth scan and says 'communicating to device', but no data transfer occurs, while NFC reading works. The thread does not establish a definitive root cause, and one affected reporter is still on Android 9.
distilled.fix: No single official fix is given.
